units.zh: 史臣曰：昔者乘雲效駕，卷領垂衣，則黃帝皁衣纁裳，放勳彤車白馬，葉三微之序，舍寅醜之建，玄戈玉刃，作會相暉。
units.en: The historiographer writes: In the legendary age, sovereigns were pictured mounting the clouds as a chariot and governing in loosely draped robes. The Yellow Emperor wore black above and reddish brown below; Yao (Fangxun) rode a vermilion chariot drawn by white horses. Rulers aligned the calendar with the “three subtle” sequence and moved away from taking Yin or Chou as the first month; black halberds and jade blades flashed together in court, each emblem answering the next in splendor.
units.literal: The historiographer says: In antiquity they rode the clouds as their chariot and wore rolled collars with hanging robes; then the Yellow Emperor had a black upper garment and crimson lower skirt, Fangxun had a cinnabar carriage and white horses; they harmonized with the sequence of the three subtle beginnings, set aside the civil month establishment of Yin and Chou, and with dark halberd and jade blade their gatherings shone one upon another.

units.zh: 若乃參旗分景，帝車含曜，又所以營衛南宮，增華北極。
units.en: The constellations Orion’s Belt and the Celestial Chariot mark off daylight and gather starlight—emblems, as it were, for protecting the southern celestial palace and crowning the northern pivot of the sky.
units.literal: As for Orion’s banner dividing the sun’s shadow and the Imperial Chariot holding radiance, these were again the means to guard the Southern Palace and add glory to the Northern Pole.

units.zh: 《月令》季夏之月，「命婦官染彩」，赬丹班次，各有品章矣。
units.en: The Monthly Ordinances for late summer command, "Order the women's offices to dye the colors"; shades of cinnabar and vermilion were sequenced by rank, each hue carrying its regulated pattern.
units.literal: In the “Monthly Ordinances,” for the last month of summer it says, “Order the women’s offices to dye the colors,” and cinnabar and red were ranked in order, each with its grades and patterns.

units.zh: 高旗有日月之象，式視有威儀之選，衣兼鞙珮，衡載鳴和，是以閑邪屏棄，不可入也。
units.en: Tall standards carried sun and moon; the chariot’s balancing crosspiece proclaimed dignity; robes were set off by belt ornaments, and the yoke bore harmonizing bells—together they shut out wickedness so that nothing base could slip through.
units.literal: High banners bore the images of sun and moon; the style of the chariot crosspiece showed selection of majesty; garments were joined with girdle-pendants, and the yoke-bar carried sounding chimes—thereby idle evil was barred and cast out and could not enter.

units.zh: 若乃正名百物，補緝四維，疏懷山之水，靜傾天之害，功尤彰者飾彌煥，德愈盛者服彌尊，莫不質良，用成其美。
units.en: When rulers set the world in order—sorting names, binding the four directions, taming floods that could swallow hills, and checking disasters that seemed to shake the heavens—the greater the achievement, the richer the regalia; the deeper the virtue, the loftier the costume. Everything was made of fine materials so that splendor matched substance.
units.literal: As for rectifying the names of the myriad things, patching the four cords, dredging the waters that threaten to engulf mountains, and quieting harms that would tilt the sky—where merit was especially manifest, ornament became especially brilliant; where virtue grew greater, dress grew more exalted; none failed to be of good substance, thereby completing their beauty.

units.zh: 《書》曰：「明試以功，車服以庸。」
units.en: The Book of Documents reads: “Test officers plainly by their work, and reward them with chariots and robes in proportion to their service.”
units.literal: The Documents says: “Clearly try them by their tasks; chariots and robes according to merit.”

units.zh: 「《禮記》曰：「鸞車，有虞氏之路也。
units.en: The Record of Rites continues: “The luan carriage was the ritual chariot of the Shun (Youyu) house.
units.literal: “The Record of Rites says: “The bell-bird carriage was the lu of the Youyu clan.

units.zh: 鉤車，夏後氏之路也。
units.en: The “hook” carriage was the ritual chariot of the Xia kings.
units.literal: The hook carriage was the lu of the Xia house.

units.zh: 大路，殷路也。
units.en: The great chariot was the Shang (Yin) ritual carriage.
units.literal: The great lu was the lu of Yin.

units.zh: 乘路，周路也。」」
units.en: The “sheng” carriage was the Zhou ritual chariot.”
units.literal: The sheng lu was the lu of Zhou.”

units.zh: 而韍火山龍，以通其意。
units.en: On robes, axe-shaped fu, fire, mountain, and dragon motifs conveyed the ruler’s intentions through regulated symbolism.
units.literal: And with fu, fire, mountain, and dragon, they communicated their intentions.

units.zh: 前史以為，聖人見鳥獸容貌，草木英華，始創衣冠，而玄黃殊采；
units.en: Earlier writers thought the sages invented hats and gowns after studying the shapes of birds and beasts and the brilliance of plants, dividing garments into dark and bright colors.
units.literal: Earlier historians held that the sages, observing the forms of birds and beasts and the splendor of plants, first created caps and robes, so that black and yellow showed different colors;

units.zh: 見秋蓬孤轉，杓觿旁建，乃作輿輪，而方圓異則。
units.en: Watching thistledown spin in the wind and noting how the Dipper and girdle-hook stars stand askew, they devised carts and wheels with distinct rules for square hubs and round felloes.
units.literal: seeing autumn thistledown whirl alone and the ladle and girdle-pick set to one side, they then made carts and wheels, so that square and round had different norms.

units.zh: 遇物成象，觸類興端。
units.en: Each thing they met suggested a design; each kind inspired a new institution.
units.literal: Encountering things, they formed images; touching categories, they raised beginnings.

units.zh: 周因于殷，其來已舊。
units.en: The Zhou built on Shang practice; the lineage of these forms was already ancient.
units.literal: Zhou inherited from Yin; its origin was already old.

units.zh: 成王之會，壇垂陰羽，五方之盛，有八十物者焉。
units.en: At King Cheng’s great gathering of lords, the ritual mound bore somber plumes, and the regalia of the five regions displayed some eighty emblematic items.
units.literal: At King Cheng’s assembly, the altar hung dark feathers, and among the splendors of the five directions there were eighty kinds of things.

units.zh: 宗馬鳥旌，奚往不格，殷公、曹叔，此焉低首。
units.en: With royal horses and bird-decked banners, every march commanded submission—even lords like the Duke of Yin and Prince Cao had to lower their heads before such majesty.
units.literal: With ancestral horses and bird streamers, whither they went none resisted; the Duke of Yin and Prince Cao of here bowed their heads.

units.zh: 《周禮》，巾車氏建大赤以朝，大白以戎。
units.en: The Zhou ritual specifies the chariot master’s raising a great scarlet banner for audiences and a great white one for military affairs.
units.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the chariot office raises the great cinnabar standard for court and the great white for war.

units.zh: 雅制弘多，式遵遺範，賓入異憲，師行殊則，是以有嚴有翼，用光其武，鉤膺鞗革，乃暢其文。
units.en: Models multiplied, yet all echoed antique precedent: guests were received under one set of rules, campaigns under another, so court looked stern and supportive while war gear flashed power—breast-straps of bronze, supple leathers—yet the same system lent polish to civil display.
units.literal: The elegant models were many; they followed the surviving patterns; guests entered under different statutes, armies marched under different rules—therefore there was awe and wing-like support, thereby displaying their martial brilliance; hooked breast-strap and leather reins, thereby giving full play to their civil refinement.

units.zh: 六服之冕，五時之路，王之常制，各有等差。
units.en: The six grades of feudal caps and the five seasonal chariot colors were fixed parts of royal ceremony, each step distinguished by rank.
units.literal: The caps of the six domains and the chariots of the five seasons were the king’s constant institutions, each with its gradations.

units.zh: 逮禮業雕訛，人情馳爽，諸侯征伐，憲度淪亡，一紫亂于齊飾，長纓混于鄒玩。
units.en: Later, as ritual frayed and ambition ran wild, vassals fought one another and regulations collapsed—a single fashionable purple threw Qi’s wardrobe into chaos, while absurdly long hat cords became playthings in Zou.
units.literal: When rites and enterprises were carved awry and human hearts raced dissolute, the feudal lords campaigned in arms and statutes perished; one purple threw Qi’s dress into confusion, and long tassels mingled with Zou’s trifles.

units.zh: 孔子曰：「君子其學也博，其服也鄉。」
units.en: Confucius remarked: “The noble man studies widely, yet his clothing stays appropriate to the customs of his own place.”
units.literal: Confucius said: “The gentleman’s learning is broad; his dress follows his home village.”

units.zh: 若乃豪傑不經，庶人幹典，彯鷸冠于鄭伯之門，躡珠履于春申之第。
units.en: Yet bold men ignored precedent and commoners flouted sumptuary law—some flaunted kingfisher-feather caps at the Zheng ruler’s gate, others wore pearl-sewn shoes in Lord Chunshen’s mansion.
units.literal: As for heroes who did not follow the classics, commoners who violated the canons, sporting kingfisher caps at the Earl of Zheng’s gate and treading pearl slippers in Lord Chunshen’s hall—

units.zh: 及秦皇並國，攬其餘軌，豐貂東至，獬豸南來，又有玄旗皁旒之制，旄頭罕車之飾，寫九王之廷於咸陽北阪，車輿之彩，各樹其文，所謂秦人大備，而陳戰國之後車者也。
units.en: When Qin Shi Huang conquered the realm, he swept up every regional fashion: sable streamed in from the east, “unicorn” judge’s caps from the south, along with black standards, sable tassels, yak-tail lances, and exotic escort cars. He staged the nine kings’ courts on Xianyang’s north terrace, each chariot type painted in its own motif—what later writers mean by “Qin had everything, down to the baggage train of the Warring States.”
units.literal: When the First Emperor of Qin united the states, he gathered what remained of their tracks; rich sable came from the east, xiezhi caps from the south; moreover there were regulations of black banners and dark tassels, ornaments of yak-tail lances and rare chariots; he copied the courts of the nine kings on the north slope of Xianyang; the colors of chariots each planted their patterns—this is what is called the Qin having full panoply and lining up the rear chariots of the Warring States.

units.zh: 及凝脂布網，經書咸燼，削滅三代，以金根為帝軫，除棄六冕，以袀玄為祭服。
units.en: After the bibliocaust, when even classics fed the flames, he tried to erase the Three Dynasties at a stroke: the “metal-root” chariot became the imperial norm, the six ancient crown types were junked, and sacrifices were conducted in austere unembroidered black.
units.literal: When congealed grease spread its net and the classics were all burned, he cut away the Three Dynasties, took the metal-root as the emperor’s axle-tree, cast off the six crowns, and used plain dark silk for sacrificial robes.

units.zh: 高祖入關，既因秦制。
units.en: When Liu Bang entered the Qin heartland, he initially kept the Qin ceremonial wardrobe and chariot codes.
units.literal: When the High Ancestor entered the Pass, he already followed Qin institutions.

units.zh: 世宗挺英雄之略，總文景之資，揚霓拂翳，皮軒記鼓，橫汾河而祠后土，登甘泉而祭昊天，奉常獻儀，謂之大駕，車千乘而騎萬匹。
units.en: Emperor Wu (Han Shizong) deployed heroic ambition on the accumulated wealth of the Wen–Jing era: iridescent banners parted the haze, leather-screen cars rolled with painted drums, he forded the Fen to worship Earth on the square mound and climbed Sweet Dew Mound to honor Heaven. The court of ritual offered the “grand chariot” array—legend speaks of a thousand cars and ten thousand riders.
units.literal: The Shizong displayed a heroic strategy, marshaled the resources of Wen and Jing, raised rainbow canopies brushing the shade, leather-screen chariots with inscribed drums, crossed the Fen River to sacrifice to Hou Tu, ascended Sweet Dew to sacrifice to August Heaven; the Minister of Ceremonies presented the models called the Grand Escort—thousands of chariots and ten thousand mounts.

units.zh: 至於成帝，以幸姬趙飛燕置屬車間豹尾中，又楊雄所謂彏天狼之威弧，張曜日之靈旄，駢羅列布，霧集雲合者也。
units.en: Emperor Cheng even tucked his favorite Zhao Feiyan’s carriage inside the leopard-tail escort—exactly the sort of spectacle Yang Xiong mocked: banners like Sirius’s war-bow, pennons blazing like the sun, vehicles massed “like mist and cloud.”
units.literal: As for Emperor Cheng, he placed his favorite, Zhao Feiyan, among the attendant cars within the leopard-tail cordon; moreover it was what Yang Xiong called drawing the mighty bow of Sirius and spreading sun-bright spirit banners, ranged side by side, gathering like fog and clouds.

units.zh: 于後王氏擅朝，武車常軔，赤眉之亂，文物無遺。
units.en: Later the Wang family hijacked government, armored columns clogged the highways, and when the Red Eyebrows swept through, the old Han ceremonial gear vanished entirely.
units.literal: Afterward the Wang clan monopolized the court, war chariots constantly blocked the roads, and in the Red Eyebrows rebellion nothing of the regalia survived.

units.zh: 建武十三年，吳漢平蜀，始送葆車輿輦，充庭之飾，漸以周備。
units.en: In Han Guangwu’s thirteenth Jianwu year, after Wu Han conquered Shu, captured Shu ceremonial wagons and litters reached the capital; bit by bit the court regained a full set of display vehicles.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jianwu, Wu Han pacified Shu and began to send treasure chariots and palanquins, court-filling ornaments, which gradually became complete.

units.zh: 明帝采《周官》、《禮記》，更服袞章，天子冠通天而佩玉璽。
units.en: Ming Di reworked court dress from the Zhou Offices and the Record of Rites, adopting the dragon-embroidered sacrificial robe; the emperor wore the tall tongtian (“pierce-heaven”) crown and carried the jade seal at his waist.
units.literal: Emperor Ming took the Zhou Offices and the Record of Rites and revised the robe with dragon roundels; the Son of Heaven capped himself with the “piercing-heaven” crown and wore the jade seal on his belt.

units.zh: 魏明以黼黻之美，有疑於僭，於是隨章儐略，而捐者半焉。
units.en: Cao Rui (Wei Ming Di), fearing that rich axe-and-fu brocade smacked of overreach, pared the wardrobe to match statute, discarding roughly half the old finery.
units.literal: Wei Ming Di, because the beauty of axe-and-fu embroidery seemed dangerously close to usurpation, then followed chapter and rank in simplifying the regalia, and half of what had been worn was cast aside.

units.zh: 高堂隆奏曰：「改正朔、殊徽號者，帝王所以神明其政，變民耳目也。」
units.en: Gao Tang Long argued: “Revising the calendar and regalia is how a ruler signals a new order and resets what the people see and hear.”
units.literal: Gao Tang Long memorialized: “Changing the first month of the year and altering emblems is how emperors make their government numinous and transform the people’s eyes and ears.”

units.zh: 帝從其議，改青龍五年為景初元年，服色尚黃，從地正也。
units.en: The throne agreed: Qinglong year five became Jingchu year one, court color turned to yellow in deference to the “earth” alignment of the calendar.
units.literal: The emperor followed his proposal, changed the fifth year of Qinglong to the first year of Jingchu, honored yellow in dress colors, following the earth’s correct alignment.

units.zh: 世祖武皇帝接天人之貺，開典午之基，受終之禮，皆如唐虞故事。
units.en: Sima Yan, the martial founding emperor, accepted heaven’s mandate and men’s allegiance, laid the Jin dynastic base—his accession rites consciously echoed the legendary abdications of Yao and Shun.
units.literal: Sima Yan, the martial founding emperor, accepted heaven’s mandate and men’s allegiance, laid the Jin dynastic base—his accession rites consciously echoed the legendary abdications of Yao and Shun.

units.zh: 晉氏金行，而服色尚赤，豈有司失其傳歟！
units.en: Jin’s element was metal, yet court dress favored red—did the ministry simply mishandle the old theory?
units.literal: The Jin house belongs to the metal phase, yet dress color honored red—could it be that the officials lost the transmission?

units.zh: 玉、金、象、革、木等路，是為五路，並天子之法車，皆硃班漆輪，畫為文。
units.en: The five ritual chariots—jade, gold, ivory, leather, and wood—form the emperor’s canonical set; each rides on red-flecked lacquer wheels painted with designs.
units.literal: Jade, gold, ivory, leather, and wood chariots—these are the five lu—and together they are the Son of Heaven’s statutory chariots; all have vermillion-spotted lacquered wheels painted with patterns.

units.zh: 三十幅，法月之數；
units.en: Thirty spokes match the lunar count;
units.literal: Thirty spokes match the number of the month;

units.zh: 重轂，貳轄，以赤油，廣八寸，長三尺，注地，系兩軸頭，謂之飛軨。
units.en: They use paired hub drums and twin linchpins, draped with red-oil cloth eight inches broad and three feet long, hanging to the ground and lashed at each axle tip—the “flying” linchpin screens.
units.literal: double hubs, paired linchpins, with red oil, eight inches wide and three feet long, dropping to the ground, tied at both axle ends—these are called flying linchpins.

units.zh: 金薄繆龍繞之為輿倚較，較重，為文獸伏軾，龍首銜軛，左右吉陽筩，鸞雀立衡，文畫轅及轓。
units.en: Gold foil dragons wrap the side rails; heavy curved “leaning” bars bear molded beasts on the front shield; dragon heads bite the yoke; lucky tubes flank the crossbar; luan birds perch on the pivot; shaft and fenders carry painted motifs.
units.literal: Thin gold sheets with intertwining dragons coil as chariot-side leaning-bars; the leaning-bars are heavy; patterned beasts crouch on the shield-grip; dragon heads hold the yoke; auspicious tubes stand left and right on the crossbar; luan birds stand on the balance; patterns are painted on the shaft and fenders.

units.zh: 青蓋，黃為裏，謂之黃屋。
units.en: The green outer canopy lined in yellow is the imperial “yellow house.”
units.literal: A green canopy with yellow inside is called the yellow house.

units.zh: 金華施橑末，橑二十八以象宿。
units.en: Gilded caps finish twenty-eight canopy ribs to mirror the lunar lodges.
units.literal: Golden splendor is applied at the rafter ends; twenty-eight rafters symbolize the lodges.

units.zh: 兩箱之後，皆玳瑁為鶤翅，加以金銀雕飾，故世人亦謂之金鶤車。
units.en: Tortoiseshell “hawk wings” trim the rear of each side box, inlaid with gold and silver—hence the nickname “golden hawk car.”
units.literal: Behind both side boxes, hawk wings are made of tortoiseshell with gold and silver carving, so worldly people also call it the golden-hawk chariot.

units.zh: 斜注旂旗于車之左，又加棨戟于車之右，皆橐而施之。
units.en: Slanted pennons ride on the car’s left, cased halberds on the right, both fixed in place.
units.literal: Banners are slanted onto the left of the chariot, and halberds are added to the right, both sheathed and mounted.

units.zh: 棨戟韜以黻繡，上為亞字，系大蛙蟆幡。
units.en: Halberd quivers wear black-and-white embroidered slips marked with a ya-shaped cross motif and fasten a large toad pennon.
units.literal: The halberds are sheathed in fu-and-xi embroidery, with an “ya” character above, tying a great toad banner.

units.zh: 軛長丈餘。
units.en: The yoke pole runs more than ten feet long.
units.literal: The yoke is over a zhang in length.

units.zh: 於戟之杪，以犛牛尾，大如鬥，置左騑馬軛上，是為左纛。
units.en: A yak tail the size of a bucket tops the halberd shaft and is fixed to the left trace horse’s yoke—the imperial “left yak-tail” ensign.
units.literal: At the tip of the halberd, a yak tail as large as a dou is placed on the left outer horse’s yoke—this is the left yak-tail banner.

units.zh: 轅皆曲向上，取《禮緯》「山車垂句」之義，言不揉而能自曲。
units.en: The shafts curve upward, echoing the omen text about “mountain cars” and drooping hooks—meaning they arc naturally without steam-bending.
units.literal: The shafts all bend upward, taking from the Ritual Weft “mountain chariot hanging hook” the meaning that they bend without being steamed.

units.zh: 玉、金、象三路，各以其物飾車，因以為名。
units.en: The jade, gold, and ivory cars are named for the materials that sheath them.
units.literal: The jade, gold, and ivory three chariots each ornament the car with its material and thereby take its name.

units.zh: 革者漆革，木者漆木。
units.en: The leather car is lacquered hide; the wood car is lacquered timber.
units.literal: Leather means lacquered leather; wood means lacquered wood.

units.zh: 其制，玉路最尊，建太常，十有二旒，九仞委地，畫日月升龍，以祀天。
units.en: Of the five, the jade chariot ranks first: it flies the Grand Constant banner with twelve streamers, nine ren of silk brushing earth, painted with sun, moon, and climbing dragon—for suburban worship of Heaven.
units.literal: In their system, the jade lu is highest; it raises the Grand Constant with twelve tassels, nine ren trailing to the ground, painting sun, moon, and ascending dragon, to sacrifice to Heaven.

units.zh: 金路建大旂，九旒，以會萬國之賓，亦以賜上公及王子母弟。
units.en: The gold car bears a nine-tasseled great banner for feasting the lords of all regions and may be awarded to chief dukes and the ruler’s uterine brothers.
units.literal: The gold lu raises the great banner with nine tassels, to assemble the myriad states’ guests, and is also conferred on senior dukes and the king’s younger brothers by the same mother.

units.zh: 象路建大赤，通赤無畫，所以視朝，亦以賜諸侯。
units.en: The ivory car flies a plain scarlet great banner—used for ordinary audiences and granted to vassal kings.
units.literal: The ivory lu raises the great cinnabar, entirely red without painting, by which to hold court, and is also conferred on feudal lords.

units.zh: 革路建大白，以即戎兵事，亦以賜四鎮諸侯。
units.en: The leather car carries the great white standard for campaign and is given to the “four guardian” marquises.
units.literal: The leather lu raises the great white, for going to war on military affairs, and is also conferred on the four-guard marquises.

units.zh: 木路建大麾，以田獵，其麾色黑，亦以賜籓國。
units.en: The wood car hoists a black hawk banner for the hunt and may be presented to outlying principalities.
units.literal: The wood lu raises the great black-falcon banner, for hunting; its banner is black in color, and is also conferred on frontier states.

units.zh: 玉路駕六黑馬，余四路皆駕四馬，馬並以黃金為文髦，插以翟尾。
units.en: The jade chariot draws six black horses; the other four draw teams of four; every horse wears gold-threaded forelocks and pheasant-tail plumes.
units.literal: The jade lu is hitched to six black horses; the remaining four chariots are all hitched to four horses; the horses all have golden patterned manes with pheasant tail plumes inserted.

units.zh: 象鑣而鏤錫，錫在馬面，所謂當顱者也。
units.en: Cheek-straps end in elephant motifs and carry pierced forehead ornaments (xi)—the metal plate on the horse’s brow.
units.literal: They have elephant-shaped cheek-pieces and openwork xi tin; the xi is on the horse’s face—what is called the “forehead metal.”

units.zh: 金㚇而方釳，
units.en: Gold zong bosses and square xi cheek plates,
units.literal: Gold zong and square xi,

units.zh: 〈金㚇謂以金㚇為文。
units.en: 〈Commentary: “Gold zong” means the bosses are patterned in gold.
units.literal: 〈Gold zong means using gold zong as pattern.

units.zh: 釳以鐵為之，其大三寸，中央兩頭高，如山形，貫中以翟尾而結著之也。〉
units.en: The xi plate is iron, three inches through the middle with raised ends like a peak, threaded with pheasant tail and bound fast.〉
units.literal: The xi is made of iron, three inches across at the center, both ends raised like a mountain shape, pierced through with pheasant tail tied and fixed.〉

units.zh: 繁纓赤罽易茸，金就十有二。
units.en: Breast tassels of red felt with soft pile, set with twelve gold studs.
units.literal: Thick tassels of red felt with easy fluff; twelve golden finials.

units.zh: 繁纓，馬飾纓，在馬膺前，如索裙。
units.en: The “thick tassels” are the chest ornaments—hanging before the saddle like a cord skirt.
units.literal: Thick tassels are the horse’s ornamental tassels, on the horse’s chest before the saddle, like a rope skirt.

units.zh: 五路皆有錫鸞之飾，和鈴之響，鉤膺玉瓖，鉤膺，即繁纓也。
units.en: All five cars carry forehead plaques and luan motifs, harmonizing bells, bronze breast-straps, and jade belt-rings—the breast-strap is the same piece as the “thick tassel” array.
units.literal: The five chariots all have xi and luan ornaments, and the sound of harmony bells; hooked breast-strap and jade huan; hooked breast-strap is the same as the thick tassels.

units.zh: 瓖，馬帶玦名也。
units.en: The huan is the jade ring on the harness band.
units.literal: Huan is the name of the horse’s belt ring.

units.zh: 龍輈華轙，輈，車轅也，頭為龍象。
units.en: The pole ends in a dragon head; “yi” refers to the splendid collar hardware.
units.literal: Dragon shaft and splendid yi; the shaft is the chariot pole, its head made in the image of a dragon.

units.zh: 轙，謂車衡上環受鸞者也。
units.en: Here “yi” is the ring on the yoke that catches the luan bird finial.
units.literal: Yi means the ring on the chariot crossbar that receives the luan.

units.zh: 硃幩。
units.en: Cinnabar-dyed fen screens.
units.literal: Cinnabar fen.

units.zh: 幩，飾也，人君以硃纏鑣扇汗，以為飾也。
units.en: “Fen” means decoration: the emperor wraps the cheek-guards’ sweat screens in vermilion thread as trim.
units.literal: Fen is ornament; the ruler uses cinnabar thread to wrap the cheek-piece fan-screen for sweat, taking it as ornament.

units.zh: 法駕行則五路各有所主，不懼出；
units.en: On a statutory progress each of the five ritual cars has its assigned role and is not deployed at random;
units.literal: When the statutory escort travels, each of the five chariots has its master and is not rashly taken out;

units.zh: 臨軒大會則陳乘輿車輦旌鼓於其殿庭。
units.en: at a great court audience the imperial cars, litters, standards, and drums line the forecourt.
units.literal: when there is a great assembly facing the hall, then the imperial chariots, palanquins, banners, and drums are arrayed in that hall’s courtyard.

units.zh: 車，坐乘者謂之安車，倚乘者謂之立車，亦謂之高車。
units.en: Chariots meant for seated riding are “peace cars”; those for standing riders are “standing cars,” also called high cars.
units.literal: Among chariots, those in which one sits to ride are called peace chariots; those in which one leans to ride are called standing chariots, also called high chariots.

units.zh: 案《周禮》，惟王后有安車也，王亦無之。
units.en: The classic Zhou text grants a seated carriage only to the queen—not even to the king.
units.literal: According to the Rites of Zhou, only the queen had a peace chariot; the king also did not have one.

units.zh: 自漢以來制乘輿，乃有之。
units.en: Only after Han codified the imperial cortège did the emperor acquire them.
units.literal: From Han onward, in instituting the imperial train, there then were such chariots.

units.zh: 有青立車、青安車、赤立車、赤安車、黃立車、黃安車、白立車、白安車、黑立車、黑安車，合十乘，名為五時車，俗謂之五帝車。
units.en: The suite includes green, red, yellow, white, and black versions in both standing and seated styles—ten cars altogether—known as the five-season set, popularly called the “Five Thearchs’ chariots.”
units.literal: There are green standing, green peace, red standing, red peace, yellow standing, yellow peace, white standing, white peace, black standing, black peace—ten chariots in all—called the five-season chariots, vulgarly termed the Five Emperors’ cars.

units.zh: 天子所禦則駕六，其餘並駕四。
units.en: The emperor’s own car draws six horses; the rest use four-horse teams.
units.literal: What the Son of Heaven personally drives is hitched to six; the rest are all hitched to four.

units.zh: 建旂十二，各如車色。
units.en: Twelve pennons fly, each dyed to match its car.
units.literal: Twelve banners are raised, each matching its chariot’s color.

units.zh: 立車則正豎其旂，安車則邪注。
units.en: Standing cars carry vertical poles; peace cars tilt their standards.
units.literal: On standing chariots the banner is set straight upright; on peace chariots it is slanted.

units.zh: 駕馬，馬亦各隨五時之色，白馬則朱其尾，左右騑驂，金㚇鏤錫，黃屋左纛，如金根之制，行則從後。
units.en: Horses are caparisoned to the five seasonal hues—white horses get vermilion tails; outriggers wear gold bosses and openwork xi, the yellow-lined canopy and left yak-tail, matching the metal-root style, and fall in behind when the train moves.
units.literal: The horses are harnessed, the horses also following the five seasons’ colors; white horses have their tails dyed vermillion; left and right trace and side horses have gold zong and openwork xi, yellow house and left yak-tail, like the metal-root system; when moving they follow behind.

units.zh: 五牛旗，平吳後所造，以五牛建旗，車設五牛，青赤在左，黃在中，白黑在右。
units.en: After Wu fell, Jin introduced the five-ox standard: five oxen support the flag, green and red to the left, yellow in the middle, white and black to the right.
units.literal: The five-ox banner was made after the pacification of Wu; with five oxen it raises the banner; the chariot sets five oxen, green and red on the left, yellow in the center, white and black on the right.

units.zh: 豎旗于牛背，行則使人輿之。
units.en: The pole stands upright on the ox; on the march bearers lift it in a portable frame.
units.literal: The banner is set vertical on the ox’s back; when moving, people carry it in a litter.

units.zh: 牛之為義，蓋取其負重致遠而安穩也。
units.en: Oxen were chosen for their steady strength over long distances.
units.literal: As for the ox’s significance, it probably takes from its bearing weight and reaching far in stability.

units.zh: 旗常纏不舒，所謂德車結旌也。
units.en: In peacetime the pennons stay furled—what ritualists call the “virtue car” with knotted streamers.
units.literal: The regular banners stay wound and are not unfurled—this is what is called the virtue chariot tying its streamers.

units.zh: 天子親戎則舒，謂武車綏旌也。
units.en: When the emperor takes the field, they spread— the “martial car” with loosened streamers.
units.literal: When the Son of Heaven personally goes to war, then they are unfurled—this is called the martial chariot relaxing its streamers.

units.zh: 金根車，駕四馬，不建旗幟，其上如畫輪車，下猶金根之飾。
units.en: The metal-root car uses four horses and no lofty standards; its upperworks resemble a painted pleasure cart, its undercarriage the metal-root trim.
units.literal: The metal-root chariot is hitched to four horses, does not raise banners, its upper part like a painted-wheel chariot, its lower part still metal-root ornament.

units.zh: 耕根車，駕四馬，建赤旂，十有二旒，天子親耕所乘者也。
units.en: The ploughing chariot, four horses, flies a twelve-tasseled red banner—the car the emperor rides to the spring furrow ritual.
units.literal: The ploughing-root chariot is hitched to four horses, raises a red banner with twelve tassels, and is what the Son of Heaven personally rides for the ploughing rite.

units.zh: 一名芝車，一名三蓋車。
units.en: It is also called the “fungus” car or the “triple-canopy” car.
units.literal: One name is zhi chariot, one name is three-canopy chariot.

units.zh: 置耒耜於軾上。
units.en: Ceremonial plough and spade rest on the front rail.
units.literal: Plow and spade are placed on the shield-grip.

units.zh: 魏景初元年，改正朔，易服色，色尚黃，牲用白，戎事乘黑首白馬，建大赤之旂，朝會則建大白，行殷之時也。
units.en: In Wei’s Jingchu inaugural year the calendar and palette were revised: yellow dominated dress, white sacrificial beasts, black-maned white horses for war, great scarlet banners on campaign, great white at audiences—deliberately echoing the Yin alignment.
units.literal: In Wei’s first Jingchu year, the first month was corrected, dress colors changed, color honored yellow, victims used white, for military affairs they rode black-headed white horses, raised the great cinnabar banner, at court meetings raised the great white, enacting Yin’s season.

units.zh: 泰始二年，有司奏：「宜如有虞遵唐故事，皆用前代正朔服色，其金根、耕根車，並以建赤旗。」
units.en: In Jin Taishi year two ministers argued: “We should imitate Shun deferring to Tang and keep the previous dynasty’s calendar and colors; metal-root and ploughing cars ought both to fly built scarlet banners.”
units.literal: In Taishi second year, the offices memorialized: “It is fitting, like Yu following Tang’s story, to use the former dynasty’s first month and dress colors; the metal-root and ploughing-root chariots should both raise built scarlet flags.”

units.zh: 帝從之。
units.en: The throne agreed.
units.literal: The emperor followed it.

units.zh: 輦，案自漢以來為人君之乘，魏晉禦小出即乘之。
units.en: The litter had been the sovereign’s short-trip vehicle since Han; Wei and Jin emperors routinely rode it for informal exits from the palace.
units.literal: The palanquin: according to custom from Han onward it was the ruler’s conveyance; Wei and Jin used it for the emperor’s short outings.

units.zh: 戎車，駕四馬，天子親戎所乘者也。
units.en: The war car, four horses, carries the emperor onto the battlefield.
units.literal: The war chariot is hitched to four horses and is what the Son of Heaven personally rides when going to war.

units.zh: 載金鼓、羽旗、幢翳，置弩於軾上，其建矛麾悉斜注。
units.en: It bears bronze drums, feathered standards, sun-shades; a crossbow mounts on the rail; spears and pennons all slant forward.
units.literal: It loads metal drums, feather banners, canopy screens; a crossbow is set on the shield-grip; its raised spears and banners are all slanted.

units.zh: 獵車，駕四馬，天子校獵所乘也。
units.en: The hunting car, four horses, serves the emperor at the great battue.
units.literal: The hunt chariot is hitched to four horses and is what the Son of Heaven rides for the encirclement hunt.

units.zh: 重輞漫輪，繆龍繞之。
units.en: It has a broad rim, fully shod wheel, and coiling dragon paint.
units.literal: Heavy rim, fully covered wheel, intertwining dragons winding it.

units.zh: 一名闒戟車，一名蹋豬車。
units.en: Also called the “halberd-rack” car or colloquially the “pig-stomper.”
units.literal: One name is halberd-bar chariot, one name is pig-tread chariot.

units.zh: 魏文帝改名蹋獸車。
units.en: Cao Pi renamed it the “beast-tread” vehicle.
units.literal: Wei Wendi changed the name to beast-tread chariot.

units.zh: 《記》云「國君不乘奇車」，奇車亦獵車也。
units.en: The classic warns that “a lord of a state does not ride strange cars”—those “strange” vehicles meant hunt wagons.
units.literal: The Record says, “A state ruler does not ride odd chariots”; odd chariots are also hunt chariots.

units.zh: 古天子獵則乘木輅，後人代以獵車也。
units.en: Ancient kings hunted from the plain wood ritual car; later courts swapped in the dedicated hunt carriage.
units.literal: In antiquity the Son of Heaven for the hunt rode the wooden lu; later men substituted the hunt chariot.

units.zh: 游車，九乘，駕四，先驅之乘是也。
units.en: Nine “patrol” cars, each with four horses, form the advance screen of the train.
units.literal: Patrol chariots, nine in number, hitched to four, are the vanguard mounts.

units.zh: 雲罕車，駕四。
units.en: The yun-han screen car rides four horses.
units.literal: The cloud-net chariot is hitched to four horses.

units.zh: 皮軒車，駕四，以獸皮為軒。
units.en: The leather-canopied escort wagon, team of four, lines its screen with pelts.
units.literal: The leather-screen chariot is hitched to four horses; it uses animal hide for the screen.

units.zh: 鸞旗車，駕四，先輅所載也。
units.en: The luan-feather banner car, four horses, rides with the vanguard train.
units.literal: The luan-banner chariot is hitched to four horses; it is what the forward lu carries.

units.zh: 鸞旗者，謂析羽旄而編之，列系幢傍也。
units.en: The “luan” standard is built from split yak plumes braided together and lashed along the canopy uprights.
units.literal: As for the luan banner, it means splitting yak-tail plumes and weaving them, arrayed and tied beside the canopy post.

units.zh: 建華車，駕四，凡二乘，行則分居左右。
units.en: Two “splendid blossom” cars, each with four horses, deploy one to each side when the column moves.
units.literal: The splendor-blossom chariot is hitched to four horses; in all there are two; when moving they are divided to left and right.

units.zh: 輕車，駕二，古之戰車也。
units.en: Light strike cars use two-horse teams—the old Zhou-style fighting wagon.
units.literal: The light chariot is hitched to two horses; it is the ancient war chariot.

units.zh: 前後二十乘，分居左右。
units.en: Twenty such cars split fore and aft between the left and right files.
units.literal: Twenty chariots front and rear are divided to left and right.

units.zh: 輿輪洞硃，不巾不蓋，建矛戟麾幢，置弩箙於軾上。
units.en: They are painted solid vermilion, open-topped, bristling with spears, halberds, and streamers, with a crossbow case fixed to the front rail.
units.literal: The body and wheels are wholly cinnabar; there is no curtain and no canopy; spears, halberds, banners, and pennons are raised; a crossbow case is placed on the shield-grip.

units.zh: 大駕法駕出，射聲校尉、司馬、吏士、戰士載，以次屬車。
units.en: Whenever the grand or statutory cortège rolls out, archery colonels, adjutants, clerks, and troops ride these as the numbered attendant cars.
units.literal: When the grand escort or statutory escort goes out, the she-sheng colonel, sima, clerks, soldiers, and warriors mount them, in order as attendant chariots.

units.zh: 司南車，一名指南車，駕四馬，其下制如樓，三級；
units.en: The south-pointing carriage—also called the compass cart—draws four horses; its body stacks three gallery levels;
units.literal: The south-pointer chariot, one name is guide chariot, is hitched to four horses; its lower structure is like a tower of three tiers;

units.zh: 四角金龍銜羽葆；
units.en: gold dragons at each corner grip feather-tasseled finials;
units.literal: At the four corners gold dragons hold feathered canopies;

units.zh: 刻木為仙人，衣羽衣，立車上，車雖回運而手常南指。
units.en: a carved immortal in feather cloak stands on deck and keeps an arm extended south no matter how the car swerves.
units.literal: Wood is carved as an immortal, clothed in a feather robe, standing on the chariot; though the chariot turns and wheels, the hand constantly points south.

units.zh: 大駕出行，為先啟之乘。
units.en: It leads the whole imperial column.
units.literal: When the grand escort goes out, it is the mount that opens the way ahead.

units.zh: 記裏鼓車，駕四，形制如司南，其中有木人執棰向鼓，行一里則打一棰。
units.en: The odometer drum car, four horses, resembles the guide carriage: a wooden figure inside beats a drum once every li traveled.
units.literal: The mile-drum chariot is hitched to four horses; its shape is like the south-pointer; inside there is a wooden man holding a mallet toward the drum; when it goes one li it strikes one blow.

units.zh: 羊車，一名輦車，其上如軺，伏兔箱，漆畫輪軛。
units.en: The “goat cart,” also called litter-style wagon, has a light upperworks like a patrol car, hare-shaped boxes, and lacquered wheels.
units.literal: The goat cart, one name is palanquin cart; its upper part is like a ya cart, with crouching-rabbit boxes, lacquered painted wheels and yoke.

units.zh: 武帝時，護軍羊琇輒乘羊車，司隸劉毅糾劾其罪。
units.en: Under Jin Wudi, Guard-general Yang Xiu habitually rode a goat-drawn cart until Liu Yi, metropolitan inspector, charged him for it.
units.literal: In Emperor Wu’s time, the household guard Yang Xiu always rode a goat cart, and the metropolitan inspector Liu Yi impeached his offense.

units.zh: 畫輪車，駕牛，以彩漆畫輪轂，故名曰畫輪車。
units.en: Ox-drawn “painted-wheel” pleasure wagons take their name from their polychrome hub decoration.
units.literal: The painted-wheel cart is drawn by oxen; because colored lacquer paints the hubs, it is therefore called the painted-wheel cart.

units.zh: 上起四夾杖，左右開四望，綠油幢，硃絲絡，青交路，其上形制事事如輦，其下猶如犢車耳。
units.en: They sport corner posts, open viewing bays, green oilcloth canopies, red mesh, and green cross-straps—upperworks like an imperial litter, lower body like a humble ox calf cart.
units.literal: Above it raises four clamped posts; left and right open four outlooks; a green-oil canopy; cinnabar silk netting; green crossing bands; on top its form in every respect is like a palanquin, while below it is still like a calf cart.

units.zh: 古之貴者不乘牛車，漢武帝推恩之末，諸侯寡弱，貧者至乘牛車，其後稍見貴之。
units.en: Classical elites scorned ox carts, but after Han’s feudal houses withered under the “extending grace” edicts, impoverished nobles took to them; over time the fashion gained respectability.
units.literal: In antiquity the noble did not ride ox carts; at the end of Emperor Wu of Han’s “extending grace” policy, the feudal lords were weak and poor, and the poor even rode ox carts; afterward they were gradually held in esteem.

units.zh: 自靈獻以來，天子至士遂以為常乘，至尊出朝堂舉哀乘之。
units.en: From the late Eastern Han emperors on, everyone up to the throne routinely used ox carts—even for sovereigns riding to court for obsequies.
units.literal: From Ling and Xian onward, from the Son of Heaven down to gentlemen they came to use them as regular conveyance; the most honored, when going out to the court hall to observe mourning, rode them.

units.zh: 屬車，一曰副車，一曰貳車，一曰左車。
units.en: Escort wagons are also termed deputy cars, second cars, or “left-side” cars in Han usage.
units.literal: Attendant chariots: one name is deputy chariot, one name is secondary chariot, one name is left chariot.

units.zh: 漢因秦制，大駕屬車八十一乘，行則中央左右分為行。
units.en: Han kept Qin’s rule of eighty-one attendant vehicles for the grand cortège, marching in center, left, and right files.
units.literal: Han followed Qin regulations: the grand escort’s attendant chariots were eighty-one; when moving, the center, left, and right divided into lines.

units.zh: 法駕屬車三十六乘。
units.en: The mid-grade statutory escort used thirty-six follow cars.
units.literal: The statutory escort’s attendant chariots were thirty-six.

units.zh: 最後車懸豹尾，豹尾以前比之省中。
units.en: The rearmost car flew a leopard-tail pennant; everything ahead of that marker counted as “within the palace” zone.
units.literal: On the hindmost chariot a leopard tail was suspended; before the leopard tail it was compared to being inside the palace.

units.zh: 屬車皆皁蓋硃裏雲。
units.en: Each escort wagon wore a black canopy lined red and painted with cloud motifs.
units.literal: Attendant chariots all had black canopies with cinnabar inside and cloud pattern.

units.zh: 御衣車、御書車、禦軺車、禦藥車，皆駕牛。
units.en: Luggage trains included robe, book, patrol, and medicine carts, all ox-drawn.
units.literal: Imperial wardrobe cart, imperial library cart, imperial patrol cart, imperial medicine cart—all were drawn by oxen.

units.zh: 陽遂四望繐窗皁輪小形車，駕牛。
units.en: Small black-wheeled “yang-sui” survey carts with gauze windows also used ox teams.
units.literal: The yang-sui four-outlook cart with coarse-silk windows, black wheels, small form, drawn by oxen.

units.zh: 象車，漢鹵簿最在前。
units.en: Han processions once led with an elephant car.
units.literal: The elephant cart was foremost in Han’s ceremonial escort.

units.zh: 武帝太康中平吳後，南越獻馴象，詔作大車駕之，以載黃門鼓吹數十人，使越人騎之。
units.en: After Jin conquered Wu in the Taikang era, Nanyue sent trained elephants; the court built huge wagons, loaded them with palace musicians, and seated southern handlers aloft.
units.literal: In Emperor Wu’s Taikang mid-period, after Wu was pacified, Southern Yue presented tame elephants; an edict ordered a great cart made to harness them, to carry several dozen yellow-gate musicians, with Yue men riding them.

units.zh: 元正大會，駕象入庭。
units.en: New Year audiences opened with elephants paraded into the palace yard.
units.literal: At the New Year’s great assembly, elephants were driven into the courtyard.

units.zh: 中朝大駕鹵簿
units.en: Western Jin capital grand cortège order (heading):
units.literal: The mid-court grand escort ceremonial guard.

units.zh: 先象車，鼓吹一部，十三人，中道。
units.en: First comes the elephant wagon and a thirteen-man front band dead center.
units.literal: First the elephant cart, one band of musicians, thirteen men, in the center way.

units.zh: 次靜室令，駕一，中道。
units.en: Then the private-chamber marshal, single car, center file.
units.literal: Next the quiet-chamber commandant, driving one, in the center way.

units.zh: 式道候二人，駕一，分左右也。
units.en: Two “road rite” inspectors follow in paired cars left and right.
units.literal: Two road-form guards, driving one each, divide left and right.

units.zh: 次洛陽尉二人，騎，分左右。
units.en: Next ride two Luoyang constables, split to the flanks.
units.literal: Next two Luoyang constables, mounted, divide left and right.

units.zh: 次洛陽亭長九人，赤車，駕一，分三道，各吹正二人引。
units.en: Nine Luoyang ward chiefs in red cars form three columns, each led by two trumpeters.
units.literal: Next nine Luoyang village headmen, red carts, driving one each, in three ways, each with two straight trumpeters leading.

units.zh: 次洛陽令，皁車，駕一，中道。
units.en: The Luoyang magistrate follows in a black official car down the center.
units.literal: Next the Luoyang magistrate, black cart, driving one, in the center way.

units.zh: 次河南中部掾，中道。
units.en: Then Henan’s central-section adjutant, center lane.
units.literal: Next the Henan central department clerk, center way.

units.zh: 河橋掾在左，功曹史在右，並駕一。
units.en: River-bridge and merit clerks pair left and right, one car each.
units.literal: The river-bridge clerk is on the left, the merit clerk on the right, both driving one each.

units.zh: 次河南尹，駕駟，戟吏六人。
units.en: The Henan governor rides a four-horse carriage with six halberd attendants.
units.literal: Next the Henan governor, driving four, six halberd clerks.

units.zh: 次河南主簿，駕一，中道。
units.en: His chief clerk follows solo in the center.
units.literal: Next the Henan chief clerk, driving one, center way.

units.zh: 次河南主記，駕一，中道。
units.en: Then the chief recorder, same formation.
units.literal: Next the Henan chief recorder, driving one, center way.

units.zh: 次司隸部河南從事，中道。
units.en: Next comes the provincial inspector’s Henan staff officer, center.
units.literal: Next the metropolitan clerk of Henan under the provincial commandant, center way.

units.zh: 都部從事居左，別駕從事居右，並駕一。
units.en: Capital-section and aide clerks split left/right with one car apiece.
units.literal: The capital-section clerk is on the left, the aide-de-camp clerk on the right, both driving one each.

units.zh: 次司隸校尉，駕三，戟吏八人。
units.en: The provincial commandant uses a three-horse car and eight halberdiers.
units.literal: Next the provincial commandant, driving three, eight halberd clerks.

units.zh: 次司隸主簿，駕一，中道。
units.en: His chief clerk rides center behind him.
units.literal: Next the provincial chief clerk, driving one, center way.

units.zh: 次司隸主記，駕一，中道。
units.en: The chief recorder mirrors that slot.
units.literal: Next the provincial chief recorder, driving one, center way.

units.zh: 次廷尉明法掾，中道。
units.en: The Court’s law-section adjutant advances down the middle.
units.literal: Next the court’s law clerk under the commandant of justice, center way.

units.zh: 五官掾居左，功曹史居右，並駕一。
units.en: Five-bureau and merit clerks flank the justice team.
units.literal: The five-bureau clerk is on the left, the merit clerk on the right, both driving one each.

units.zh: 次廷尉卿，駕駟，戟吏六人。
units.en: The commandant of justice rides four horses with six halberds.
units.literal: Next the commandant of justice, driving four, six halberd clerks.

units.zh: 次廷尉主簿、主記，並駕一，在左。
units.en: Court chief clerk and recorder share a left-side car.
units.literal: Next the court chief clerk and chief recorder, both driving one, on the left.

units.zh: 太僕引從如廷尉，在中。
units.en: The grand coachman’s train matches the court layout, centered.
units.literal: The grand coachman’s escort follows like the commandant of justice, in the center.

units.zh: 宗正引從如廷尉，在右。
units.en: The imperial-clan director mirrors the court on the right.
units.literal: The director of the imperial clan’s escort follows like the commandant of justice, on the right.

units.zh: 次太常，駕駟，中道，戟吏六人。
units.en: The grand master of rites rides four-in-hand down the axis with six halberds.
units.literal: Next the grand master of ceremonies, driving four, center way, six halberd clerks.

units.zh: 太常外部掾居左，五官掾、功曹吏居右，並駕一。
units.en: His external and bureau clerks split the line behind him.
units.literal: The grand master of ceremonies’ external clerk is on the left, the five-bureau and merit clerks on the right, both driving one each.

units.zh: 次光祿引從，中道。
units.en: The household superintendent’s escort fills the center next.
units.literal: Next the superintendent of the household escort, center way.

units.zh: 太常主簿、主記居左，衛尉引從居右，並駕一。
units.en: Ritual clerks ride left while the guard commandant’s party rides right.
units.literal: The grand master of ceremonies’ chief clerk and chief recorder are on the left, the commandant of the guard’s escort on the right, both driving one each.

units.zh: 次太尉外督令史，駕一，中道。
units.en: The marshal’s exterior clerk follows solo center.
units.literal: Next the grand marshal’s external order clerk, driving one, center way.

units.zh: 次西東賊倉戶等曹屬，並駕一，引從。
units.en: East and west “bandit” and granary bureau aides trail in single cars.
units.literal: Next the western and eastern bandit and granary household bureau subordinates, all driving one each, leading and following.

units.zh: 次太尉，駕駟，中道。
units.en: The grand marshal’s four-horse state coach anchors the center.
units.literal: Next the grand marshal, driving four, center way.

units.zh: 太尉主簿、舍人各一人，祭酒二人，並駕一，在左。
units.en: His chief clerk, chamberlain, and two libationers share left-side mounts.
units.literal: The grand marshal’s chief clerk and houseman one each, two libationers, all driving one, on the left.

units.zh: 次司徒引從，駕駟，中道。
units.en: The grand tutor follows with the same four-horse dignity.
units.literal: Next the grand tutor’s escort, driving four, center way.

units.zh: 次司空引從，駕駟，中道。
units.en: The minister of works repeats the pattern.
units.literal: Next the grand minister of works’ escort, driving four, center way.

units.zh: 三公騎令史戟各八人，鼓吹各一部，七人。
units.en: Each of the three dukes rates eight mounted clerks with halberds plus a seven-man band.
units.literal: The three excellencies’ mounted order clerks each have eight men with halberds, each one band of musicians, seven men.

units.zh: 次中護軍，中道，駕駟。
units.en: The central army guardian rides four abreast on the axis.
units.literal: Next the central guardian of the army, center way, driving four.

units.zh: 鹵簿左右各二行，戟楯在外，弓矢在內，鼓吹一部，七人。
units.en: His guard forms twin files: shields outward, archers inward, plus a seven-piece band per side.
units.literal: On each side of the escort two rows, halberd shields on the outside, bows and arrows on the inside, one band of musicians, seven men.

units.zh: 次步兵校尉在左，長水校尉在右，並駕一。
units.en: Infantry and “long-shore” colonels pair left and right.
units.literal: Next the infantry colonel on the left, the long-shore colonel on the right, both driving one each.

units.zh: 各鹵簿左右二行，戟楯在外，刀楯在內，鼓吹各一部，七人。
units.en: Each colonel’s screen repeats halberd outer, blade-shield inner, with bands.
units.literal: Each escort has left and right two rows, halberd shields on the outside, knife shields on the inside, each one band of musicians, seven men.

units.zh: 次射聲校尉在左，翊軍校尉在右，並駕一。
units.en: Archery and “assisting army” colonels split the next rank.
units.literal: Next the archery-sound colonel on the left, the assisting-army colonel on the right, both driving one each.

units.zh: 各鹵簿左右各二行，戟楯在外，刀楯在內，鼓吹各一部，七人。
units.en: Their formations mirror the previous pair.
units.literal: Each escort left and right each two rows, halberd shields on the outside, knife shields on the inside, each one band of musicians, seven men.

units.zh: 次驍騎將軍在左，遊擊將軍在右，並駕一。
units.en: Fierce cavalry and mobile-strike generals take the following slots.
units.literal: Next the fierce-cavalry general on the left, the roaming-strike general on the right, both driving one each.

units.zh: 皆鹵簿左右引各二行，戟楯在外，刀楯在內，鼓吹各一部，七人。
units.en: Each general’s escort again fields paired files with musicians.
units.literal: All escorts left and right each have two leading rows, halberd shields on the outside, knife shields on the inside, each one band of musicians, seven men.

units.zh: 騎隊，五在左，五在右，隊各五十匹，命中督二人分領左右。
units.en: Ten cavalry squadrons of fifty mounts each split five and five under two strike directors.
units.literal: Mounted squadrons: five on the left, five on the right; each squadron fifty horses, two strike colonels separately commanding left and right.

units.zh: 各有戟吏二人，麾幢獨揭，鼓在隊前。
units.en: Every squadron posts halberd aides, lone streamers, and drums ahead.
units.literal: Each has two halberd clerks; banners and pennons are raised singly; drums stand before the squadron.

units.zh: 次左將軍在左，前將軍在右，並駕一。
units.en: Left and forward generals ride paired cars next.
units.literal: Next the general of the left on the left, the forward general on the right, both driving one each.

units.zh: 皆鹵簿左右各二行，戟楯盾在外，刀楯在內，鼓吹各一部，七人。
units.en: Their guards add large shields outside, blade shields inside, plus bands.
units.literal: All escorts left and right each two rows, halberd shields and shields on the outside, knife shields on the inside, each one band of musicians, seven men.

units.zh: 次黃門麾騎，中道。
units.en: Yellow-gate mounted escorts tighten the center file.
units.literal: Next yellow-gate standard cavalry, center way.

units.zh: 次黃門前部鼓吹，左右各一部，十三人，駕駟。
units.en: Palace musicians split thirteen-player bands per side on four-horse wagons.
units.literal: Next yellow-gate front musicians, left and right each one band, thirteen men, driving four.

units.zh: 八校尉佐仗，左右各四行，外大戟楯，次九尺楯，次弓矢，次弩，並熊渠、佽飛督領之。
units.en: Eight colonels’ guards stack four ranks apiece—great halberds, nine-foot shields, bows, then crossbows—under specialist colonels.
units.literal: The eight colonels’ auxiliary halberds: left and right each four rows, great halberd shields on the outside, next nine-chi shields, next bows and arrows, next crossbows, all led by bear-channel and flying-strike colonels.

units.zh: 次司南車，駕駟，中道。
units.en: The guide carriage returns to the axis, four horses.
units.literal: Next the south-pointer chariot, driving four, center way.

units.zh: 護駕御史，騎，夾左右。
units.en: Imperial censors ride flanking the guide car.
units.literal: Attendant imperial censors, mounted, flanking left and right.

units.zh: 次謁者僕射，駕駟，中道。
units.en: The master of ceremonies for audiences follows four-in-hand.
units.literal: Next the supervisor of attendants, driving four, center way.

units.zh: 次御史中丞，駕一，中道。
units.en: The imperial secretary rides a single state car center.
units.literal: Next the palace secretary supervisor, driving one, center way.

units.zh: 次武賁中郎將，騎，中道。
units.en: Next the rapid household guard general canters down the middle.
units.literal: Next the household rapid guard general, mounted, center way.

units.zh: 次九游車，中道，武剛車夾左右，並駕駟。
units.en: Nine “excursion” cars march center with armored “martial” wagons on both flanks.
units.literal: Next nine excursion chariots, center way, martial-hard chariots flanking left and right, both driving four.

units.zh: 次雲罕車，駕駟，中道。
units.en: The yun-han car repeats, four horses center.
units.literal: Next the cloud-net chariot, driving four, center way.

units.zh: 次闒戟車，駕駟，中道，長戟邪偃向後。
units.en: Halberd-rack cars follow, spears raked rearward.
units.literal: Next the halberd-rack chariot, driving four, center way, long halberds slanted backward.

units.zh: 次皮軒車，駕駟，中道。
units.en: Leather-screen escort wagons close up the center.
units.literal: Next the leather-screen chariot, driving four, center way.

units.zh: 次鸞旗車，中道，建華車分左右，並駕駟。
units.en: Luan-banner cars hold the axis while twin “splendid blossom” cars fan out.
units.literal: Next the luan-banner chariot, center way; splendor-blossom chariots divide left and right, both driving four.

units.zh: 次護駕尚書郎三人，都官郎中道，駕部在左，中兵在右，並騎。
units.en: Three ministerial escort riders—capital, equipage, and army bureaus—split center, left, and right.
units.literal: Next three household guardian gentlemen of the masters of writing: the capital bureau gentleman center way, the equipage bureau on the left, the central army bureau on the right, all mounted.

units.zh: 又有護駕尚書一人，騎，督攝前後無常。
units.en: A roving ministerial rider coordinates the whole segment.
units.literal: Moreover there is one household guardian gentleman of the masters of writing, mounted, supervising front and rear without fixity.

units.zh: 次相風，中道。
units.en: A wind-reading device rolls up the center.
units.literal: Next the wind-reading vane, center way.

units.zh: 次司馬督，在前，中道。
units.en: Marshal supervisors advance at the head of the block.
units.literal: Next the marshal supervisor, in front, center way.

units.zh: 左右各司馬史三人引仗，左右各六行，外大戟楯二行。
units.en: Marshal clerks lead six-deep files with great halberd shields outermost.
units.literal: Left and right each three marshal clerks leading halberds; left and right each six rows; outside great halberd shields two rows.

units.zh: 次九尺楯，次刀楯。
units.en: Nine-foot shields precede blade shields.
units.literal: Next nine-chi shields, next knife shields.

units.zh: 次弓矢，次弩。
units.en: Archers step before crossbowmen.
units.literal: Next bows and arrows, next crossbows.

units.zh: 次五時車，左右有遮列騎。
units.en: Five-season cars ride with cordon cavalry on each side.
units.literal: Next the five-season chariots; left and right have screening column cavalry.

units.zh: 次典兵中郎，中道，督攝前卻無常。
units.en: An arms-bureau officer roves the line regulating pace.
units.literal: Next the arms bureau gentleman, center way, supervising advance and retreat without fixity.

units.zh: 左殿中御史，右殿中監，並騎。
units.en: Palace censor left, palace intendant right, both ahorse.
units.literal: Left palace censor, right palace intendant, both mounted.

units.zh: 次高蓋，中道，左罼，右罕。
units.en: High umbrellas march center flanked by bi and han feather screens.
units.literal: Next tall canopy, center way, left bi net, right han net.

units.zh: 次御史，中道，左右節郎各四人。
units.en: Imperial censors advance on the axis, flanked by four section cadets per side.
units.literal: Next the censor, center way, left and right four section gentlemen each four men.

units.zh: 次華蓋，中道。
units.en: A great flowered umbrella follows on the center line.
units.literal: Next the flowered canopy, center way.

units.zh: 次殿中司馬，中道。
units.en: The palace marshal’s detail rides dead center.
units.literal: Next the palace marshal, center way.

units.zh: 殿中都尉在左，殿中校尉在右，左右各四行。
units.en: Palace commandant left, palace colonel right, each with four ranks of guards.
units.literal: The palace commandant is on the left, the palace colonel on the right; left and right each have four rows.

units.zh: 細楯一行在弩內，又殿中司馬一行，殿中都尉一行，殿中校尉一行。
units.en: Inside the archers stands a file of light shields, then marshals, commandants, and colonels each in their own row.
units.literal: One row of small shields inside the crossbows, again one row of palace marshals, one row of palace commandants, one row of palace colonels.

units.zh: 次扌罡鼓，中道。
units.en: Next roll the long-handled processional drums straight down the middle.
units.literal: Next roll the long-handled processional drums straight down the middle.

units.zh: 次金根車，駕六馬，中道。
units.en: The emperor’s six-horse metal-root car occupies the axis.
units.literal: Next the metal-root chariot, hitched to six horses, center way.

units.zh: 太僕卿禦，大將軍參乘。
units.en: The grand coachman holds the reins while the grand general sits beside him.
units.literal: The grand coachman drives; the grand general is riding companion.

units.zh: 左右又各增三行，為九行。
units.en: Three extra files join each flank, widening the screen to nine deep.
units.literal: Left and right each add three rows, making nine rows.

units.zh: 司馬史九人，引大戟楯二行，九尺楯一行，刀楯一行，由基一行，細弩一行，跡禽一行，椎斧一行，力人刀楯一行。
units.en: Nine adjutants shepherd stacked ranks: great halberds, nine-foot shields, blade shields, elite Youji bowmen, light crossbows, tracker squads, axe parties, and heavy infantry with shields.
units.literal: Nine marshal clerks lead two rows of great halberd shields, one row of nine-chi shields, one row of knife shields, one row of Youji archers, one row of fine crossbows, one row of game trackers, one row of maul-axes, one row of strong men with knife shields.

units.zh: 連細楯，殿中司馬，殿中都尉，殿中校尉，為左右各十二行。
units.en: Light shields tie the formation to palace marshals, commandants, and colonels—twelve files on each side.
units.literal: Linking small shields, palace marshals, palace commandants, palace colonels, for left and right each twelve rows.

units.zh: 金根車建青旂十二。
units.en: The imperial car flies twelve green streamers.
units.literal: The metal-root chariot raises twelve green banners.

units.zh: 左將軍騎在左，右將軍騎在右，殿中將軍持鑿腦斧夾車，車後衣書主職步從，六行，合左右三十二行。
units.en: Left and right generals pace the flanks while palace generals brace the car with axe guards; wardrobe and archive clerks trail on foot in six columns—thirty-two ranks in all.
units.literal: The general of the left rides on the left, the general of the right on the right; palace generals hold notched battle-axes hugging the car; behind the car wardrobe and library clerks walk in attendance, six rows; together left and right make thirty-two rows.

units.zh: 次曲華蓋，中道。
units.en: A domed flowered umbrella closes over the sovereign.
units.literal: Next the curved flowered canopy, center way.

units.zh: 侍中、散騎常侍、黃門侍郎並騎，分左右。
units.en: Palace intimates—attendants-in-ordinary and yellow-gate gentlemen—split left and right on horseback.
units.literal: Attendant-in-ordinary, cavalry attendant-in-ordinary, and yellow-gate gentleman riders all mounted, dividing left and right.

units.zh: 次黃鉞車，駕一，在左，禦麾騎在右。
units.en: A single car bears the gilded axe leftward while standard-bearing riders hold the right.
units.literal: Next the yellow battle-axe chariot, driving one, on the left; the imperial standard cavalry on the right.

units.zh: 次相風，中道。
units.en: Another wind vane marks the center.
units.literal: Next the wind-reading vane, center way.

units.zh: 次中書監騎左，秘書監騎右。
units.en: Secretariat and palace library directors bracket the column.
units.literal: Next the secretariat director rides left, the palace library director rides right.

units.zh: 次殿中御史騎左，殿中監騎右。
units.en: Palace censor to the left, palace intendant to the right.
units.literal: Next the palace censor rides left, the palace intendant rides right.

units.zh: 次五牛旗，赤青在左，黃在中，白黑在右。
units.en: The five-ox standard returns with its fixed color positions.
units.literal: Next the five-ox banner, red and green on the left, yellow in the center, white and black on the right.

units.zh: 次大輦，中道。
units.en: The great imperial litter follows on the axis.
units.literal: Next the great palanquin, center way.

units.zh: 太官令丞在左，太醫令丞在右。
units.en: Court caterers ride left, court physicians right of the litter.
units.literal: The grand provisioner director and aide are on the left, the grand physician director and aide on the right.

units.zh: 次金根車，駕駟，不建旗。
units.en: A second metal-root car, four horses, flies no tall standards.
units.literal: Next the metal-root chariot, driving four, not raising banners.

units.zh: 次青立車，次青安車，次赤立車，次赤安車，次黃立車，次黃安車，次白立車，次白安車，次黑立車，次黑安車，合十乘，並駕駟。
units.en: Ten five-season cars follow in order—green, red, yellow, white, and black, each in standing and seated styles—all four-horse teams.
units.literal: Next green standing chariot, next green peace chariot, next red standing, next red peace, next yellow standing, next yellow peace, next white standing, next white peace, next black standing, next black peace—ten chariots in all—all driving four.

units.zh: 建旗十二，如車色。
units.en: Twelve pennons are dyed to match their cars.
units.literal: Twelve banners are raised, matching the chariot colors.

units.zh: 立車正豎旗，安東邪拖之。
units.en: Standing cars fly vertical poles; seated cars trail their banners at an angle.
units.literal: Standing cars fly vertical poles; seated cars trail their banners at an angle.

units.zh: 次蹋豬車，駕駟，中道，無旗。
units.en: The low hunt wagon (pig-tread style) follows four-in-hand, unbannered.
units.literal: Next the pig-tread chariot, driving four, center way, without banners.

units.zh: 次耕根車，駕駟，中道，赤旗十二，熊渠督左，佽飛督右。
units.en: The ploughing car rides four abreast with twelve scarlet streamers, flanked by bear-channel and flying-strike colonels.
units.literal: Next the ploughing-root chariot, driving four, center way, twelve red banners, bear-channel colonel on the left, flying-strike colonel on the right.

units.zh: 次禦軺車，次禦四望車，次御衣車，次御書車，次禦藥車，並駕牛，中道。
units.en: Ox-drawn imperial service wagons—patrol, survey, wardrobe, archive, and pharmacy—string along the center.
units.literal: Next the imperial patrol cart, next the imperial four-outlook cart, next the imperial wardrobe cart, next the imperial library cart, next the imperial medicine cart—all drawn by oxen, center way.

units.zh: 次尚書令在左，尚書僕射在右，又尚書郎六人，分次左右，並駕。
units.en: The minister and vice-minister of the masters of writing lead, with six secretaries split to either flank, all riding.
units.literal: Next the masters of writing director on the left, the vice director on the right, again six masters of writing gentlemen, dividing in order left and right, all mounted.

units.zh: 又治書侍御史二人，分左右，又侍御史二人，分次左右，又蘭台令史分次左右，並騎。
units.en: Supervising censors, attending censors, and orchid-terrace clerks mirror the same left-right pairing on horseback.
units.literal: Again two supervising secretaries attending censors divide left and right; again two attending censors divide in order left and right; again orchid terrace clerks divide in order left and right, all mounted.

units.zh: 次豹尾車，駕一。
units.en: The leopard-tail escort car rides alone.
units.literal: Next the leopard-tail chariot, driving one.

units.zh: 自豹尾車後而鹵簿盡矣。
units.en: Behind the leopard-tail wagon the formal cortège ends.
units.literal: From behind the leopard-tail chariot the ceremonial guard is complete.

units.zh: 但以神弩二十張夾道，至後部鼓吹。
units.en: Yet twenty heavy crossbows still line the route rearward to the trailing bands.
units.literal: But twenty divine crossbows line the road on both sides, reaching to the rear musicians.

units.zh: 其五張神弩置一將，左右各二將。
units.en: Each five-piece battery has its own captain, two captains to a side.
units.literal: For every five divine crossbows one commander is posted; left and right each have two commanders.

units.zh: 次輕車二十乘，左右分駕。
units.en: Twenty light wagons split evenly to the flanks.
units.literal: Next twenty light chariots, left and right separately driving.

units.zh: 次流蘇馬六十匹。
units.en: Sixty horses with silk tassels follow.
units.literal: Next sixty tassel horses.

units.zh: 次金鉞車，駕三，中道。
units.en: A three-horse gilded-axe car rides center.
units.literal: Next the golden battle-axe chariot, driving three, center way.

units.zh: 左右護駕尚書郎並令史，並騎，各一人。
units.en: Ministerial escort riders and clerks bracket the axe car, one rider each side.
units.literal: Left and right household guardian masters of writing gentlemen and clerks, all mounted, each one man.

units.zh: 次金鉦車，駕三，中道。
units.en: A three-horse gilded gong wagon comes next on the axis.
units.literal: Next the golden gong chariot, driving three, center way.

units.zh: 左右護駕侍御史並令史等，並騎，各一人。
units.en: Censorial escorts and clerks mirror the gong car left and right.
units.literal: Left and right household guardian attending censors and clerks, all mounted, each one man.

units.zh: 次黃門後部鼓吹，左右各十三人。
units.en: Rear palace bands post thirteen players per flank.
units.literal: Next yellow-gate rear musicians, left and right thirteen men each.

units.zh: 次戟鼓車，駕牛，二乘，分左右。
units.en: Two ox-drawn drum-and-halberd wagons split to the sides.
units.literal: Next halberd-drum carts, drawn by oxen, two chariots, dividing left and right.

units.zh: 次左大鴻臚外部掾，右五官掾、功曹史，並駕。
units.en: Grand herald aides ride left; five-bureau and merit clerks right.
units.literal: Next the left grand herald external clerk, the right five-bureau and merit clerks, all mounted.

units.zh: 次大鴻臚，駕駟，鉞吏六人。
units.en: The grand herald of guests rides four-in-hand with six axemen.
units.literal: Next the grand herald, driving four, six axe clerks.

units.zh: 次大司農引從，中道，左大鴻臚主簿、主記，右少府引從。
units.en: The minister of finance centers the block while herald and household ministers trail their staffs on either side.
units.literal: Next the grand minister of agriculture leading followers, center way; left grand herald chief clerk and chief recorder, right minister of the less palace leading followers.

units.zh: 次三卿，並騎，吏四人，鈴下二人，執馬鞭辟車六人，執方扇羽林十人，硃衣。
units.en: The three senior ministers ride with clerks, bell pages, road-clearers with whips, ten feather-fan guards in red.
units.literal: Next the three ministers, all mounted, four clerks, two bell attendants, six men holding horse whips clearing the road, ten imperial guard men with square fans, cinnabar robes.

units.zh: 次領軍將軍，中道。
units.en: The commanding general closes the center file.
units.literal: Next the commanding general of the army, center way.

units.zh: 鹵簿左右各二行，九尺楯在外，弓矢在內，鼓吹如護軍。
units.en: His screen repeats the army-guard pattern—nine-foot shields out, archers in, matched bands.
units.literal: The escort left and right each two rows, nine-chi shields on the outside, bows and arrows on the inside, musicians like the guardian of the army.

units.zh: 次後軍將軍在左，右將軍在右，各鹵簿鼓吹如左軍、前軍。
units.en: Rear and right army generals mirror the left and forward army formations.
units.literal: Next the rear army general on the left, the right general on the right; each escort and musicians like the left army and forward army.

units.zh: 次越騎校尉在左，屯騎校尉在右，各鹵簿鼓吹如步兵、射聲。
units.en: Yue and encampment cavalry colonels copy the infantry and archery colonels’ layouts.
units.literal: Next the colonel of Yue cavalry on the left, the colonel of encampment cavalry on the right; each escort and musicians like the infantry and archery-sound colonels.

units.zh: 次領護驍騎、游軍校尉，皆騎，吏四人，乘馬夾道，都督兵曹各一人，乘馬在中。
units.en: Colonels of fierce and roaming guards ride with clerks lining the avenue while bureau overseers hold the middle.
units.literal: Next the colonels leading and guarding fierce cavalry and roaming army, all mounted, four clerks, riding horses lining the road, army and bureau overseers each one man riding in the center.

units.zh: 騎將軍四人，騎校、鞉角、金鼓、鈴下、信幡、軍校並駕一。
units.en: Mounted generals and colonels share cars with drummers, horn players, gongs, pages, signal flags, and adjutants.
units.literal: Four mounted generals, mounted colonels, hand-drums, horns, metal drums, bell attendants, signal banners, and army clerks each drive one.

units.zh: 功曹吏、主簿並騎從。
units.en: Chief and merit clerks follow on horseback.
units.literal: Merit clerks and chief clerks all mounted in attendance.

units.zh: 扇幢麾各一騎，鼓吹一部，七騎。
units.en: Each fan, canopy, and standard gets a rider; bands number seven horsemen.
units.literal: Fan, canopy, and banner each one rider; one band of musicians, seven riders.

units.zh: 次領護軍，加大車斧，五官掾騎從。
units.en: The commanding guardian rides with great cart axes and five-bureau escorts.
units.literal: Next the commanding guardian of the army, adding great cart axes, five-bureau clerks mounted in attendance.

units.zh: 次騎十隊，隊各五十匹。
units.en: Ten cavalry troops of fifty mounts apiece follow.
units.literal: Next ten cavalry squadrons, each squadron fifty horses.

units.zh: 將一人，持幢一人，鞉一人，並騎在前，督戰伯長各一人，並騎在後，羽林騎督、幽州突騎督分領之。
units.en: Each troop fronts a commander, standard bearer, and drummer, with overseers and chiefs riding rear; forest cavalry and Youzhou shock colonels split leadership.
units.literal: One commander, one man holding a canopy, one drummer, all mounted in front; battle overseers and squad chiefs each one man, all mounted behind; feather-forest cavalry colonel and Youzhou shock cavalry colonel divide command of them.

units.zh: 郎簿十隊，隊各五十人。
units.en: Ten fifty-man gentleman guard companies march behind.
units.literal: Gentleman guard ten squads, each squad fifty men.

units.zh: 絳袍將一人，騎、鞉各一人，在前，督戰伯長各一人，步，在後。
units.en: Crimson-clad commanders lead mounted drummers while foot overseers bring up the rear.
units.literal: One crimson-robed commander, mounted, one drummer in front, battle overseers and squad chiefs each one man on foot behind.

units.zh: 騎皆持槊。
units.en: Every rider carries a lance.
units.literal: The cavalry all hold lances.

units.zh: 次大戟一隊，九尺楯一隊，刀楯一隊，弓一隊，弩一隊，隊各五十人。
units.en: Infantry blocks follow: halberdiers, nine-foot shieldmen, blade shields, bowmen, and crossbowmen—fifty each.
units.literal: Next one squad of great halberds, one squad of nine-chi shields, one squad of knife shields, one squad of bows, one squad of crossbows; each squad fifty men.

units.zh: 黑袴褶將一人，騎校、鞉角各一人，步，在前，督戰伯長各一人，步，在後。
units.en: Black-uniform commanders head each block with mounted colonels and horn players ahead, overseers afoot behind.
units.literal: One black-trouser commander, mounted colonel and horn each one man on foot in front, battle overseers and squad chiefs each one man on foot behind.

units.zh: 金顏督將並領之。
units.en: Inspector colonels (gold-visored officers) jointly command these files.
units.literal: The gold-visored colonels jointly lead them.

units.zh: 皇太子安車，駕三，左右騑。
units.en: The crown prince’s seated carriage uses three horses with outriggers.
units.literal: The heir apparent’s peace chariot is hitched to three horses, left and right trace horses.

units.zh: 硃班輪，倚獸較，伏鹿軾。
units.en: Vermillion-flecked wheels, animal-carved leaning rails, and a deer motif on the front shield.
units.literal: Vermillion-spotted wheels, leaning bars with crouching beasts, shield-grip with crouching deer.

units.zh: 九旒，畫降龍。
units.en: Nine streamers bear painted descending dragons.
units.literal: Nine tassels, painting descending dragon.

units.zh: 青蓋，金華蚤二十八枚。
units.en: A green canopy carries twenty-eight gilded rib caps.
units.literal: Green canopy, golden splendor nails twenty-eight pieces.

units.zh: 黑文畫轓，文輈，黃金塗五采。
units.en: Black scrollwork trims the fenders; the pole is patterned and gilded in five colors.
units.literal: Black patterns paint the fenders, patterned shaft, five colors overlaid with gold.

units.zh: 亦謂之鸞路。
units.en: Courtiers also call it the heir’s “luan” carriage.
units.literal: It is also called the luan lu.

units.zh: 非法駕則乘畫輪車，上開四望，綠油幢，硃絲繩絡，兩箱裏飾以金錦，黃金塗五采。
units.en: On informal outings he uses the painted-wheel survey car—open galleries, green canopy, red mesh, gold brocade lining the boxes, polychrome gilding.
units.literal: If not the statutory ride, then he rides the painted-wheel cart, opening four outlooks above, green-oil canopy, cinnabar silk netting, both side boxes inside ornamented with gold brocade, gold overlaid with five colors.

units.zh: 其副車三乘，形制如所乘，但不畫輪耳。
units.en: Three escort cars match his train except their wheels stay unpainted.
units.literal: His deputy chariots are three; the form is like what he rides, but they do not paint the wheels.

units.zh: 王青蓋車，皇孫綠蓋車，並駕三，左右騑。
units.en: Princes ride green-canopy cars; imperial grandsons use a greener shade—both three-horse with outriggers.
units.literal: Princes’ green-canopy chariot, imperial grandsons’ green-canopy chariot, both hitched to three, left and right trace horses.

units.zh: 雲母車，以雲母飾犢車。
units.en: The “mica wagon” plates a calf cart with mica panels.
units.literal: The mica chariot uses mica to ornament the calf cart.

units.zh: 臣下不得乘，以賜王公耳。
units.en: Only kings and dukes receive this honor; lower ranks may not use it.
units.literal: Subordinates may not ride it; it is conferred on dukes and princes only.

units.zh: 皁輪車，駕四牛，形制猶如犢車，但皁漆輪轂，上加青油幢，硃絲繩絡。
units.en: The black-wheel ox cart resembles a calf car but for jet-black wheels, green oilcloth roof, and red mesh.
units.literal: The black-wheel chariot is drawn by four oxen; its form is still like a calf cart, but wheels and hubs are lacquered black, with green-oil canopy above and cinnabar silk netting.

units.zh: 諸王三公有勳德者特加之。
units.en: The throne awards it only to meritorious princes and three excellencies.
units.literal: Princes and three dukes who have merit and virtue are specially granted it.

units.zh: 位至公或四望、三望、夾望車。
units.en: Dukes may graduate to multi-outlook survey wagons as rank allows.
units.literal: Those who reach duke rank may receive four-outlook, three-outlook, or flanked-outlook chariots.

units.zh: 油幢車，駕牛，形制如皁輪，但不漆轂耳。
units.en: Oil-canopy ox carts match black-wheel style except the hubs stay plain.
units.literal: The oil-canopy chariot is drawn by oxen; its form is like the black-wheel, but it does not lacquer the hubs.

units.zh: 王公大臣有勳德者特給之。
units.en: Meritorious dukes and senior ministers alone receive these vehicles.
units.literal: Dukes, princes, and great ministers who have merit and virtue are specially given them.

units.zh: 通幰車，駕牛，猶如今犢車制，但舉其幰通覆車上也。
units.en: The “through-curtain” ox cart works like a modern calf car but drapes a continuous awning over the top.
units.literal: The open-curtain chariot is drawn by oxen; it is still like today’s calf cart system, but it lifts its curtain to cover the whole car above.

units.zh: 諸王三公並乘之。
units.en: All princes and three excellencies may use this type.
units.literal: The various princes and three dukes all ride them.

units.zh: 諸公給朝車駕四、安車黑耳駕三各一乘，皁輪犢車各一乘。
units.en: Dukes receive a four-horse court car, a three-horse black-eared peace car, and a black-wheel calf cart apiece.
units.literal: The various dukes are given court chariots driving four, peace chariots with black ears driving three, one each, and black-wheel calf carts one each.

units.zh: 自祭酒掾屬以下及令史，皆皁零，辟朝服。
units.en: From libationer aides down to archivists everyone rides black-canopied carts and wears full court robes.
units.literal: From libationer aides down to archivists everyone rides black-canopied carts and wears full court robes.

units.zh: 其武官公又別給大車。
units.en: Generals who hold ducal rank also receive heavy supply wagons.
units.literal: Martial office dukes are separately given great carts.

units.zh: 特進及車騎將軍驃騎將軍以下諸大將軍不開府非持節都督者，給安車黑耳駕二，軺車施耳後戶一乘。
units.en: Senior nobles and full generals short of independent commands get two-horse peace cars plus a single patrol wagon with ear screens and a rear door.
units.literal: For fully eminent nobles and grand generals of chariot and cavalry, swift cavalry, and below who do not open offices and are not area commanders with credentials, they are given peace chariots with black ears driving two, and one patrol cart with ears and rear door.

units.zh: 三公、九卿、中二千石、二千石、河南尹、謁者僕射、郊廟明堂法出，皆大車立乘，駕駟。
units.en: For state rituals the three dukes, nine ministers, full two-thousand-bushel officials, the Luoyang governor, and the master of ceremonies ride standing in four-horse state wagons.
units.literal: The three excellencies, nine ministers, those at two thousand piculs full and regular, the Henan governor, the supervisor of attendants, for statutory outings to suburban altars, bright hall, and law processions, all use great carts standing to ride, driving four.

units.zh: 前後導從大車駕二，右騑。
units.en: Their escorts use two-horse wagons with a right outrigger.
units.literal: Front and rear guides and followers use great carts driving two, right trace horse.

units.zh: 他出乘安車。
units.en: On ordinary business they switch to seated carriages.
units.literal: For other outings they ride peace chariots.

units.zh: 其去位致仕告老，賜安車駟馬。
units.en: Retiring officials receive a honorific four-horse peace car.
units.literal: Those who leave office, retire, or announce old age are granted peace chariots and four horses.

units.zh: 郡縣公侯，安車駕二，右騑。
units.en: County-level nobles ride two-horse peace cars with a right trace.
units.literal: District, county, dukes, and marquises: peace chariot driving two, right trace horse.

units.zh: 皆硃班輪，倚鹿較，伏熊軾，黑輜，皁繒蓋。
units.en: Their cars share vermilion-flecked wheels, deer-carved rails, bear motifs on the shield, black coachwork, and sable canopies.
units.literal: All have vermillion-spotted wheels, leaning bars with crouching deer, shield-grip with crouching bear, black carriage box, black silk canopy.

units.zh: 公旗旂八旒，侯七旒，卿五旒，皆畫降龍。
units.en: Ducal standards carry eight streamers, marquis seven, minister five—each with descending dragons.
units.literal: Dukes’ banners and flags have eight tassels, marquises seven, ministers five, all painting descending dragons.

units.zh: 中二千石、二千石，皆皁蓋，硃兩轓，銅五采，駕二。
units.en: Two-thousand-bushel officials use black tops, red paired fenders, bronze five-color trim, and two-horse teams.
units.literal: Those at two thousand piculs full and regular, and two thousand piculs, all have black canopies, cinnabar two fenders, bronze five colors, driving two.

units.zh: 中二千石以上，右騑。
units.en: Full two-thousand ranks add a right-side outrigger.
units.literal: Those above full two thousand piculs have the right trace horse.

units.zh: 千石、六百石，硃左轓。
units.en: Lower salaried ranks mark only the left fender in vermilion.
units.literal: One thousand piculs and six hundred piculs have cinnabar left fender.

units.zh: 車轓長六尺，下屈廣八寸，上業廣尺二寸，九丈，十二初，後謙一寸，若月初生，示不敢自滿也。
units.en: Fenders measure six chi along the curve, eight cun at the bend, twelve cun at the crown, with nine-zhang silk and twelve pleats; the rear tip cuts inward one cun like a new moon to symbolize modesty.
units.literal: The chariot fender is six chi long; the lower bend is eight cun wide; the upper edge is one chi two cun wide; nine zhang, twelve beginnings; the rear modest one cun, like the new moon’s first crescent, showing not daring to be self-full.

units.zh: 王公之世子攝命理國者，安車，駕三，旗旂七旒，其封侯之世子五旒。
units.en: Princely heirs who govern draw three-horse peace cars with seven streamers; marquis’ heirs use five.
