units.literal: Heir sons of kings and dukes who hold office and administer the state have peace chariots driving three, banners and flags with seven tassels; heir sons enfeoffed as marquises have five tassels.

units.zh: 太康四年，制：「依漢故事，給九卿朝車駕四及安車各一乘。」
units.en: Taikang year four issued: “Follow Han practice—grant each of the nine ministers a four-horse court wagon plus one peace car.”
units.literal: In the fourth year of Taikang, the regulation said: “According to Han precedent, give the nine ministers court chariots driving four and peace chariots one each.”

units.zh: 八年，詔：「諸尚書軍校加侍中常侍者，皆給傳事乘軺車，給劍，得入殿省中，與侍臣升降相隨。」
units.en: Eight years later an edict added: “Secretariat army aides who also hold attendant-in-ordinary titles receive fast patrol cars and swords so they may enter palace corridors and move with the inner court.”
units.literal: In the eighth year, an edict said: “For various masters of writing army clerks who add attendant-in-ordinary or cavalry attendant-in-ordinary, all give courier duty riding patrol carts, give swords, allowing entry to palace halls, ascending and descending with attendant officials.”

units.zh: 大使車，立乘，駕四，赤帷裳，騶騎導從。
units.en: Senior envoys use tall four-horse cars with crimson drapery and mounted escorts opening the road.
units.literal: The great envoy chariot is ridden standing, hitched to four, red curtains and skirts, outriders clearing the way.

units.zh: 舊公卿二千石郊廟上陵從駕，乘大使車，他出乘安車也。
units.en: Han rules had two-thousand-bushel nobles stand in the great envoy wagon for state sacrifices and tomb rites, then switch to seated cars elsewhere.
units.literal: Formerly dukes and ministers at two thousand piculs for suburban altars, imperial tombs, and following the chariot rode the great envoy chariot; for other outings they rode peace chariots.

units.zh: 小使車，不立乘，駕四，輕車之流也。
units.en: The “small envoy” model is a seated four-horse light carriage.
units.literal: The small envoy chariot is not ridden standing; it is hitched to four; it is of the light chariot class.

units.zh: 蘭輿皆硃，赤轂，赤屏泥，白蓋，赤帷裳，從騶騎四十人。
units.en: “Orchid” escort wagons are scarlet with red wheels, white tops, red hangings, and forty outriders.
units.literal: Orchid carts are all vermillion, red hubs, red mud-screens, white canopy, red curtains and skirts; forty mounted escorts follow.

units.zh: 又別有小使車，赤轂皁蓋，追捕考案有所執取者之所乘也。
units.en: A darker variant with black canopy serves police inspectors on arrests and inquests.
units.literal: Moreover there is separately a small envoy chariot, red hubs and black canopy, for those who pursue, capture, investigate, and take persons into custody to ride.

units.zh: 凡諸使車皆硃班輪，赤衡軛。
units.en: All official messenger cars share vermilion-flecked wheels and red yoke hardware.
units.literal: In general the various envoy chariots all have vermillion-spotted wheels and red crossbar and yoke.

units.zh: 追鋒車，去小平蓋，加通幰，如軺車，駕二。
units.en: “Swift-fringe” couriers strip the small roof for a full awning like a patrol car and use two horses.
units.literal: The swift-fringe chariot removes the small flat canopy, adds a through-curtain, like a patrol cart, hitched to two.

units.zh: 追鋒之名，蓋取其迅速也，施於戎陣之間，是為傳乘。
units.en: The name signals speed; on campaign it serves as the dash relay vehicle.
units.literal: The name swift-fringe probably takes from its speed; applied within battle arrays, this is called relay riding.

units.zh: 軺車，古之時軍車也。
units.en: Patrol cars descend from Han military runabouts.
units.literal: The patrol cart was in antiquity the army chariot.

units.zh: 一馬曰軺車，二馬曰軺傳。
units.en: One-horse models are “patrol cars”; paired teams are “patrol relays.”
units.literal: One horse is called patrol cart; two horses is called patrol relay.

units.zh: 漢世貴輜軿而賤軺車，魏晉重軺車而賤輜軿。
units.en: Han fashion favored closed sedans; Wei–Jin reversed the prestige to light patrol cars.
units.literal: Han generations esteemed enclosed wagons and disdained patrol carts; Wei and Jin esteemed patrol carts and disdained enclosed wagons.

units.zh: 三品將軍以上、尚書令軺車黑耳有後戶，僕射但有後戶無耳，並皁輪。
units.en: Generals of third rank and the minister of state get black-eared patrol cars with back doors; vice ministers lose the “ears” but keep the rear hatch—all on black wheels.
units.literal: For third-rank generals and above and the masters of writing director, the patrol cart has black ears and a rear door; the vice director has only a rear door without ears; both have black wheels.

units.zh: 尚書及四品將軍則無後戶，漆轂輪。
units.en: Fourth-rank officers ride simpler patrol wagons without rear doors but lacquered hubs.
units.literal: For masters of writing and fourth-rank generals there is no rear door; hubs and wheels are lacquered.

units.zh: 其中書監令如僕射，侍中、黃門、散騎，初拜及謁陵廟，亦得乘之。
units.en: Secretariat directors, attendants-in-ordinary, and yellow-gate nobles may use these cars for first appointments and tomb pilgrimages.
units.literal: For secretariat director and vice like the vice director, attendant-in-ordinary, yellow gate, and cavalry attendant-in-ordinary, on first appointment and when visiting imperial tombs they also may ride them.

units.zh: 皇太后、皇后法駕，乘重翟羽蓋金根車，駕青輅，青帷裳，雲畫轅，黃金塗五采，蓋爪施金華，駕三，左右騑。
units.en: The two highest ladies ride stacked kingfisher canopies on metal-root frames, green ritual cars, cloud-painted poles, gilded fittings, three gray horses with outriggers.
units.literal: For the empress dowager and empress statutory escort, they ride the layered kingfisher-feather canopy metal-root chariot, hitched to green lu, green curtains and skirts, cloud-painted shaft, gold overlaid with five colors; canopy claws apply golden splendor; hitched to three, left and right trace horses.

units.zh: 其廟見小駕，則乘紫罽軿車，雲畫輈，黃金塗五采，駕三。
units.en: For lesser ritual they switch to purple felt sedans with three-horse teams.
units.literal: For temple audiences with the small escort, they ride the purple felt enclosed wagon, cloud-painted pole, gold overlaid with five colors, hitched to three.

units.zh: 非法駕則皇太后乘輦，皇后乘畫輪車。
units.en: Informal outings put the dowager in a litter and the empress in a painted-wheel survey car.
units.literal: If not the statutory ride, then the empress dowager rides a palanquin and the empress rides a painted-wheel chariot.

units.zh: 皇后先蠶，乘油畫雲母安車，駕六騩馬；
units.en: The silkworm ceremony uses an oil-painted mica peace car with six dapple-gray mounts;
units.literal: For the empress’s first silkworm rite she rides an oil-painted mica peace chariot, hitched to six gui horses;

units.zh: 騩，淺黑色。
units.en: “Gui” denotes blue-black horses.
units.literal: Gui means light black.

units.zh: 油畫兩轅安車，駕五騩馬，為副。
units.en: A five-horse twin-shaft duplicate trails as escort.
units.literal: An oil-painted two-shaft peace chariot, hitched to five gui horses, serves as deputy.

units.zh: 又，金薄石山軿、紫絳罽軿車，皆駕三騩馬，為副。
units.en: Gold-foil “stone mountain” sedans and purple felt cars follow with three-horse teams.
units.literal: Moreover, thin-gold stone-mountain enclosed wagons and purple-red felt enclosed wagons are all hitched to three gui horses as deputies.

units.zh: 女旄頭十二人，持棨戟二人，共載安車，儷駕。
units.en: Twelve female yak-tail runners pair-drive a support peace car with two halberdiers aboard.
units.literal: Twelve women yak-tail guards, two holding halberds, together load a peace chariot, paired hitch.

units.zh: 女尚輦十二人，乘輜車，儷駕。
units.en: Twelve litter maids ride closed wagons in paired teams.
units.literal: Twelve women palanquin attendants ride enclosed wagons, paired hitch.

units.zh: 女長禦八人，乘安車，儷駕。
units.en: Eight senior maids drive their own peace cars, paired.
units.literal: Eight women chief drivers ride peace chariots, paired hitch.

units.zh: 三夫人油軿車，駕兩馬，左騑。
units.en: The three chief consorts use oilcloth sedans, two horses plus a left outrigger.
units.literal: The three consorts ride oil enclosed wagons, hitched to two horses, left trace horse.

units.zh: 其貴人駕節畫輈。
units.en: Lower-ranked noble ladies get simpler pole decoration.
units.literal: The honored ladies drive festival-painted poles.

units.zh: 三夫人助蠶，乘青交路，安車，駕三，皆以紫絳罽軿車。
units.en: At the consorts’ silkworm aid they take green-banded three-horse peace cars with purple felt duplicates.
units.literal: The three consorts assisting at silkworm rite ride green crossing-band peace chariots, hitched to three, all using purple-red felt enclosed wagons.

units.zh: 九嬪世婦乘軿車，駕三。
units.en: Nine concubines and chief wives ride three-horse sedans.
units.literal: The nine concubines and noble wives ride enclosed wagons, hitched to three.

units.zh: 長公主赤罽軿車，駕兩馬。
units.en: Senior princesses use crimson felt two-horse sedans.
units.literal: The senior princess rides a red felt enclosed wagon, hitched to two horses.

units.zh: 公主、王太妃、王妃，皆油軿車，駕兩馬，右騑。
units.en: Imperial princesses and princely consorts take oilcloth sedans with two horses and a right trace.
units.literal: Princesses, royal grand consorts, and princes’ consorts all ride oil enclosed wagons, hitched to two horses, right trace horse.

units.zh: 公主油畫安車，駕三，青交路，以紫絳罽軿車駕三為副，王太妃、三夫人亦如之。
units.en: Princesses’ formal three-horse cars match grand consorts’ and chief consorts’ purple felt escorts.
units.literal: Princesses’ oil-painted peace chariots are hitched to three with green crossing bands, using purple-red felt enclosed wagons hitched to three as deputies; royal grand consorts and the three consorts are the same.

units.zh: 公主助蠶，乘油畫安車，駕三。
units.en: Princesses at the silkworm rite use three-horse painted peace cars.
units.literal: Princesses assisting at silkworm ride oil-painted peace chariots, hitched to three.

units.zh: 公主有先置者，乘青交路安車，駕三。
units.en: Princesses already invested ride green-banded three-horse peace wagons.
units.literal: Princesses who have prior placement ride green crossing-band peace chariots, hitched to three.

units.zh: 諸王妃、公太夫人、夫人、縣鄉君、諸郡公侯特進夫人助蠶，乘皁交路安車，駕三。
units.en: Princely consorts through county noblewomen ride black-banded three-horse peace cars at silkworm.
units.literal: The various princes’ consorts, ducal grand ladies, ladies, county and district noblewomen, and the various commandery dukes’ and marquises’ eminent ladies assisting at silkworm ride black crossing-band peace chariots, hitched to three.

units.zh: 諸侯監國世子之世婦、侍中常侍尚書中書監令卿校世婦、命婦助蠶，乘皁交路安車，儷駕。
units.en: Heirs’ wives and high inner-court ladies use black-banded peace cars with paired teams.
units.literal: Feudal heirs’ chief wives supervising the state, palace attendant-in-ordinary and cavalry attendant-in-ordinary masters of writing secretariat director and vice ministers’ chief wives, and titled ladies assisting at silkworm ride black crossing-band peace chariots, paired hitch.

units.zh: 郡縣公侯、中二千石、二千石夫人會朝及蠶，各乘其夫之安車，皆右騑，皁交路，皁帷裳。
units.en: Noblewives attend court and silkworm in their husbands’ two-horse peace cars with black trim and right outriggers.
units.literal: County and district dukes and marquises, and wives of full and regular two thousand piculs, for court meetings and silkworm each ride their husbands’ peace chariots, all with right trace horse, black crossing bands, black curtains and skirts.

units.zh: 自非公會則不得乘軺車，止乘漆布輜軿，銅五采而已。
units.en: Outside assemblies they must use lacquered cloth sedans, not patrol cars.
units.literal: Unless for public meetings they may not ride patrol carts, only lacquered cloth enclosed wagons, bronze five colors only.

units.zh: 王妃、特進夫人、封郡君，安車，駕三，皁交路。
units.en: High consorts and commandery ladies rate three-horse black-banded peace cars.
units.literal: Princes’ consorts, eminent ladies, and commandery noblewomen have peace chariots, hitched to three, black crossing bands.

units.zh: 封縣鄉君油軿車，駕兩馬，右騑。
units.en: County-level titled women use oilcloth two-horse sedans with right traces.
units.literal: County and district noblewomen ride oil enclosed wagons, hitched to two horses, right trace horse.

units.zh: 自過江之後，舊章多缺。
units.en: Once the court fled south, most old sumptuary rules collapsed.
units.literal: After crossing the Yangzi, old regulations were mostly lacking.

units.zh: 元帝踐極，始造大路、戎路各一，皆即古金根之制也，無復充庭之儀。
units.en: Emperor Yuan commissioned one great chariot and one war car on old metal-root lines but skipped the full Han panoply.
units.literal: When Yuan Di ascended the throne, he first made a great lu and a war lu, each one, both following the ancient metal-root system, without again the court-filling display.

units.zh: 至於郊祀大事，則權飾余車以周用。
units.en: Major suburban rites borrowed patched-up spare wagons.
units.literal: As for suburban sacrifice great affairs, then they temporarily ornamented spare chariots to suffice for use.

units.zh: 六師親征則用戎路，去其蓋而乘之，屬車但五乘而已。
units.en: Field armies stripped the war car’s roof and cut the escort to five vehicles.
units.literal: When the six armies personally campaigned they used the war lu, removed its canopy and rode it; attendant chariots were only five in number.

units.zh: 加綠油幢，硃絲路，飾青交路，黃金塗五采，其輪轂猶素，兩箱無金錦之飾。
units.en: Campaign gear added green canopies and red mesh but left wheels plain and sides unbroidered.
units.literal: They added green-oil canopy, cinnabar silk netting, ornamented green crossing bands, gold overlaid with five colors; their wheels and hubs were still plain; the two side boxes lacked gold brocade ornament.

units.zh: 其一車又是軺車，舊儀，天子所乘駕六，是時無復六馬之乘，五路皆駕四而已，同用黑，是為玄牡。
units.en: Even the patrol wagon drew four blacks; the old six-horse emperor’s team vanished—everything went four-in-hand in ink-dark bays.
units.literal: One of the chariots was again a patrol cart; by old ritual the Son of Heaven rode six, but at this time there was no longer riding six horses; the five chariots all were hitched to four only, together using black—this is the dark stallion set.

units.zh: 無復五時車，有事則權以馬車代之，建旗其上。
units.en: Five-season colors gave way to improvised carts flying temporary standards.
units.literal: There were no longer five-season chariots; when there was business they temporarily substituted horse carts, raising banners on them.

units.zh: 其後但以五色木牛象五時車，豎旗于牛背，行則使人輿之。
units.en: Later designers painted wooden ox teams to mimic the old five-color parade.
units.literal: Afterward they only used five-colored wooden oxen to imitate the five-season chariots, setting banners on the oxen’s backs; when moving they had people carry them in litters.

units.zh: 牛之義，蓋取其負重致遠安而穩也。
units.en: Oxen again symbolized steady haulage.
units.literal: As for the ox’s significance, it probably takes from its bearing weight and reaching far in peace and stability.

units.zh: 旗常纏而不舒旆，所謂德車結旌者也。
units.en: Pennants stayed furled—the “virtue car” look.
units.literal: The regular banners stay wound and do not unfurl pennants—this is called the virtue chariot tying its streamers.

units.zh: 惟天子親戎，五旗舒旆，所謂武車綏旌者也。
units.en: Only the emperor at war spread all five battle streamers.
units.literal: Only when the Son of Heaven personally went to war did the five banners unfurl pennants—this is called the martial chariot relaxing its streamers.

units.zh: 指南車，過江亡失，及義熙五年，劉裕屠廣固，始復獲焉，乃使工人張綱補緝周用。
units.en: The guide car sank in the retreat until Liu Yu’s Yixi sack of Guanggu recovered one for Zhang Gang to rebuild.
units.literal: The south-pointer chariot was lost crossing the Yangzi; and in the fifth year of Yixi, Liu Yu sacked Guanggu and only then recovered it, then ordered the craftsman Zhang Gang to patch and mend it for temporary use.

units.zh: 十三年，裕定關中，又獲司南、記裏諸車，制度始備。
units.en: Thirteen years later Liu Yu’s Guanzhong campaign brought back odometer cars, completing the set.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year, Yu pacified Guanzhong and again obtained south-pointer and mile-drum chariots; only then were the institutions complete.

units.zh: 其輦，過江亦亡制度，太元中謝安率意造焉，及破苻堅於淮上，獲京都舊輦，形制無差，大小如一，時人服其精記。
units.en: Litters were reinvented by Xie An until, after defeating Fu Jian on the Huai, a captured Luoyang litter proved his memory flawless.
units.literal: As for the palanquin, crossing the Yangzi also lost its institutions; in the Taiyuan period Xie An improvised one; and when he defeated Fu Jian at the Huai, he obtained the old capital palanquin, and the form and size were without difference, of one size; people of the time admired his precise memory.

units.zh: 義熙五年，劉裕執慕容超，獲金鉦輦、豹尾，舊式猶存。
units.en: Yixi five’s capture of Murong Chao yielded gilded gong litters and leopard-tail regalia intact.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Yixi, Liu Yu seized Murong Chao and obtained gilded-gong palanquins and leopard tails; the old style still survived.

units.zh: 元帝太興三年，皇太子釋奠。
units.en: Taixing year three saw the crown prince’s Confucian ceremony.
units.literal: In the third year of Emperor Yuan’s Taixing, the heir apparent performed the school sacrifice.

units.zh: 制曰：「今草創，未有高車，可乘安車也。」
units.en: The edict admitted: “We are still improvising—use peace cars until tall state coaches exist.”
units.literal: The regulation said: “Now in founding beginnings, there are no high chariots; you may ride peace chariots.”

units.zh: 太元中，東宮建，乘路有青赤旂，致疑。
units.en: Later, when the heir got his own chariots, mixed green and red standards confused ritualists.
units.literal: In the Taiyuan period, when the eastern palace was built, riding lu had green and red banners, raising doubts.

units.zh: 徐邈議，太子既不備五路，赤旂宜省。
units.en: Xu Miao ruled the prince should drop scarlet banners without the full five-car set.
units.literal: Xu Miao argued that since the heir did not possess the five chariots, the red banner should be omitted.

units.zh: 漢制，太子鸞路皆以安車為名。
units.en: Han had always called the heir’s ritual car a peace-style luan.
units.literal: Han institutions named all heir apparent luan lu with peace chariot.

units.zh: 自晉過江，禮儀疏舛，王公以下，車服卑雜，惟有東宮禮秩崇異，上次辰極，下納侯王。
units.en: Southern Jin dress codes frayed for everyone except the heir, whose regalia alone rivaled the throne.
units.literal: Since Jin crossed the Yangzi, ritual was sparse and mixed; from kings and dukes downward, chariots and dress were lowly and miscellaneous; only the eastern palace ritual rank was lofty and different, ascending next to the pole star, downward admitting marquises and kings.

units.zh: 而安帝為皇太子乘石山安車，制如金路，義不經見，事無所出。
units.en: An Di’s odd stone-mountain peace car aping the metal lu lacked classical warrant.
units.literal: Yet when Emperor An was crown prince he rode a stone-mountain peace chariot, regulated like the metal lu; righteousness does not appear in the classics, and the matter has no source.

units.zh: 中宮初建及祀先蠶，皆用法駕，太僕妻禦，大將軍妻參乘，侍中妻陪乘，丹陽尹建康令及公卿之妻奉引，各乘其夫車服，多以宮人權領其職。
units.en: Empress silkworm rites drafted noblewomen as drivers and outriders—coachmen’s wives at the reins, generals’ wives beside them, magistrates’ wives clearing the way, often palace women standing in.
units.literal: When the inner palace was first built and for sacrificing to the first silkworm, all used the statutory escort; the grand coachman’s wife drove, the grand general’s wife rode companion, the attendant-in-ordinary’s wife rode attendant; the Danyang governor, Jiankang magistrate, and dukes’ and ministers’ wives led the train, each riding their husbands’ chariot dress, mostly using palace women temporarily filling those posts.

units.zh: 《周禮》，弁師掌六冕，司服掌六服。
units.en: Zhou ritual split crown and robe oversight between two ministries.
units.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the cap master controls the six crowns, and the dress master controls the six robes.

units.zh: 自後王之制爰及庶人，各有等差。
units.en: Every rank down to commoners once had fixed wardrobe rules.
units.literal: From later kings’ institutions down to commoners, each had grades and differences.

units.zh: 及秦變古制，郊祭之服皆以袀玄，舊法掃地盡矣。
units.en: Qin’s plain black sacrifice robes erased Zhou splendor.
units.literal: When Qin changed ancient institutions, suburban sacrifice dress all used plain dark silk, and old law was swept clean.

units.zh: 漢承秦弊，西京二百餘年猶未能有所制立。
units.en: Western Han still had no stable court wardrobe two centuries on.
units.literal: Han inherited Qin’s abuses, and for more than two hundred years in Western Capital still could not establish institutions.

units.zh: 及中興後，明帝乃始采《周官》、《禮記》、《尚書》及諸儒記說，還備袞冕之服。
units.en: Eastern Han Ming Di rebuilt sacrificial dress from Zhou texts and scholars’ notes.
units.literal: After the restoration, Emperor Ming then first took the Zhou Offices, Record of Rites, Documents, and various scholars’ records, and returned to complete the robe and crown with hanging tassels.

units.zh: 天子車乘冠服從歐陽氏說，公卿以下從大小夏侯氏說，始制天子、三公、九卿、特進之服，侍祠天地明堂，皆冠旒冕，兼五冕之制，一服而已。
units.en: Ming Di split sources—Ouyang for the emperor, Xiahou masters for officials—unifying heaven, earth, and hall rites under one tasseled crown system.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven’s chariots, caps, and robes followed Master Ouyang’s theory; from dukes and ministers downward followed the greater and lesser Xiahou theory; he first regulated the Son of Heaven, three excellencies, nine ministers, and fully eminent nobles’ dress; when attending sacrifice to heaven and earth, bright hall, all wore tasseled crowns and held the five-crown system in one robe.

units.zh: 天子備十二章，三公諸侯用山龍九章，九卿以下用華蟲七章，皆具五采。
units.en: The emperor wore twelve symbolic motifs; dukes nine; ministers seven—each in full five-color embroidery.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven fully had twelve emblems; three excellencies and feudal lords used mountain and dragon nine emblems; nine ministers downward used flower-and-insect seven emblems; all possessed five colors.

units.zh: 魏明帝以公卿袞衣黼黻之飾，疑於至尊，多所減損，始制天子服刺繡文，公卿服織成文。
units.en: Cao Rui demoted ministerial brocade to woven patterns while reserving true embroidery for the throne.
units.literal: Wei Ming Di, because dukes’ and ministers’ sacrificial robes had axe-and-fu ornament, suspected encroachment on the supreme; he reduced much; he first regulated the Son of Heaven’s robes with embroidered patterns, dukes’ and ministers’ robes with woven patterns.

units.zh: 及晉受命，遵而無改。
units.en: Jin kept Wei’s wardrobe partition.
units.literal: When Jin received the mandate, it followed without change.

units.zh: 天子郊祀天地明堂宗廟，元會臨軒，黑介幘，通天冠，平冕。
units.en: The Jin emperor wears black frame cap under the tongtian crown and flat sacrificial mian crown for heaven, hall, temple, and New Year.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven for suburban sacrifice to heaven and earth, bright hall, and ancestral temples, and for the great New Year session facing the hall, wears black stiff cap, piercing-heaven crown, and level crown.

units.zh: 冕，皁表，硃綠裏，廣七寸，長二尺二寸，加于通天冠上，前圓後方，垂白玉珠，十有二旒，以硃組為纓，無緌。
units.en: The flat mian crown is black with vermilion-green lining, twelve white jade tassels, round-squared profile, cinnabar ties, no trailing fringe.
units.literal: The crown (mian) is black outside, cinnabar and green inside, seven cun wide, two chi two cun long, placed on the piercing-heaven crown, round in front and square behind, hanging white jade beads, twelve tassels, with cinnabar cords for tassels, without dangling threads.

units.zh: 佩白玉，垂珠黃大旒，綬黃赤縹紺四采。
units.en: White jade pendants, yellow tassel strings, four-color sash.
units.literal: He wears white jade, hanging pearls with great yellow tassels, sash of yellow, red, light blue, and dark blue four colors.

units.zh: 衣皁上，絳下，前三幅，後四幅，衣畫而裳繡，為日、月、星辰、山、龍、華蟲、藻、火、粉米、黼、黻之象，凡十二章。
units.en: The upper robe is dyed with the twelve cosmic emblems; the lower skirt embroiders matching motifs.
units.literal: The robe is black above, crimson below, three panels in front, four in back; the robe is painted and the skirt is embroidered, with images of sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragons, flower-and-insect, waterweed, fire, powdered grain, fu, and fu—twelve emblems in all.

units.zh: 素帶廣四寸，硃裏，以硃綠裨飾其側。
units.en: A four-inch white belt is lined red with vermilion-green edge strips.
units.literal: The plain belt is four cun wide, cinnabar inside, using cinnabar and green borders to ornament its sides.

units.zh: 中衣以絳緣其領袖。
units.en: The under-robe cuffs and collar are piped in scarlet.
units.literal: The middle garment uses crimson to border its collar and cuffs.

units.zh: 赤皮為韍，絳袴襪，赤舄。
units.en: Red leather kneecaps, scarlet hose, crimson shoes.
units.literal: Red leather for knee covers, crimson trousers and socks, red shoes.

units.zh: 未加元服者，空頂介幘。
units.en: Uncapped heirs wear open mesh frames.
units.literal: Those who have not yet added the capping use empty-top stiff caps.

units.zh: 其釋奠先聖，則皁紗袍，絳緣中衣，絳袴襪，黑舄，其臨軒，亦袞冕也。
units.en: Confucian rites use black gauze with scarlet borders; court audiences revert to full mian regalia.
units.literal: For sacrificing to the former sage, then black gauze robe, crimson-bordered middle garment, crimson trousers and socks, black shoes; for facing the hall, also robe and crown with tassels.

units.zh: 其朝服，通天冠高九寸，金博山顏，黑介幘，絳紗袍，皁緣中衣。
units.en: Daily court dress pairs a nine-inch tongtian crown with gold brow plate and scarlet gauze robe.
units.literal: For court dress, the piercing-heaven crown is nine cun high, with golden Bo Mountain on the brow, black stiff cap, cinnabar gauze robe, black-bordered middle garment.

units.zh: 其拜陵，黑介幘，單衣。
units.en: Tomb pilgrimages simplify to black cap and plain robe.
units.literal: For visiting tombs, black stiff cap, unlined garment.

units.zh: 其雜服，有青赤黃白緗黑色，介幘，五色紗袍，五梁進賢冠，遠遊冠，平上幘武冠。
units.en: Leisure wardrobes span six hues with five-ridge scholar caps, touring caps, and martial headcloths.
units.literal: For miscellaneous dress there are green, red, yellow, white, light yellow, and black colors, stiff caps, five-color gauze robes, five-ridge worthy-advancement cap, far-roaming cap, level-top martial cap, martial cap.

units.zh: 其素服，白㡊單衣。
units.en: Mourning dress is white headcloth over unlined coat.
units.literal: For plain mourning dress, white kerchief and unlined garment.

units.zh: 後漢以來，天子之冕，前後旒用真白玉珠。
units.en: Later Han emperors insisted on real white jade beads for the royal mian crown.
units.literal: From Later Han onward, the Son of Heaven’s crown front and rear tassels used genuine white jade beads.

units.zh: 魏明帝好婦人之飾，改以珊瑚珠。
units.en: Cao Rui famously swapped jade for coral beads.
units.literal: Wei Ming Di liked women’s ornaments and changed them to coral beads.

units.zh: 晉初仍舊不改。
units.en: Early Jin kept coral.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jin it still followed the old without change.

units.zh: 及過江，服章多闕，而冕飾以翡翠珊瑚雜珠。
units.en: Southern courts patched mian regalia with jadeite and coral mixes.
units.literal: After crossing the Yangzi, dress insignia were mostly lacking, yet the crown ornaments used kingfisher, coral, and mixed beads.

units.zh: 侍中顧和奏：「舊禮，冕十二旒，用白玉珠。
units.en: Gu He pleaded: “Classical mian crowns need twelve white jade strands.
units.literal: Attendant-in-ordinary Gu He memorialized: “By old ritual the crown has twelve tassels using white jade beads.

units.zh: 今美玉難得，不能備，可用白璿珠。」
units.en: He allowed white spinel substitutes when Hetian jade ran short.”
units.literal: Now fine jade is hard to obtain and cannot be supplied; white spinel pearls may be used.”

units.zh: 從之。
units.en: The throne agreed.
units.literal: The emperor followed it.

units.zh: 通天冠，本秦制。
units.en: The tongtian crown began as Qin court gear.
units.literal: The piercing-heaven crown was originally a Qin institution.

units.zh: 高九寸，正豎，頂少斜卻，乃直下，鐵為卷梁，前有展筒，冠前加金博山述，乘輿所常服也。
units.en: Nine inches tall with iron curl, forward “sounding tube,” and gold brow plate—it is everyday imperial headgear.
units.literal: It is nine cun high, set straight, the top slightly slanting backward, then straight down, iron forming the curled beam, with a spreading tube in front; the crown front adds golden Bo Mountain description; it is what the imperial carriage regularly wears.

units.zh: 平冕，王公、卿助祭於郊廟服之。
units.en: Princes and ministers wear the flat mian crown only at joint sacrifices.
units.literal: The level crown: kings, dukes, and ministers wear it when assisting sacrifice at suburban altars and temples.

units.zh: 王公八旒，卿七旒。
units.en: Princes get eight tassels, chief ministers seven.
units.literal: Kings and dukes have eight tassels; ministers seven tassels.

units.zh: 以組為纓，色如其綬。
units.en: Tassel cords match each man’s sash colors.
units.literal: They use cords for tassels, the color like their sash.

units.zh: 王公衣山龍以下九章，卿衣華蟲以下七章。
units.en: Princely robes stop at nine motifs; ministers at seven.
units.literal: Kings and dukes’ robes have mountain and dragon down to nine emblems; ministers’ robes have flower-and-insect down to seven emblems.

units.zh: 遠遊冠，傅玄雲秦冠也。
units.en: Fu Xuan traces the “far roaming” cap to Qin fashion.
units.literal: The far-roaming cap: Fu Xuan says it is a Qin cap.

units.zh: 似通天而前無山述，有展筒橫於冠前。
units.en: Like tongtian but without the gold brow mountain, with a horizontal tube across the brim.
units.literal: It resembles the piercing-heaven but lacks the mountain description in front; there is a spreading tube spanning before the crown.

units.zh: 皇太子及王者後、帝之兄弟、帝之子封郡王者服之。
units.en: Crown princes, princely heirs, imperial brothers, and sons enfeoffed as kings wear this cap.
units.literal: The heir apparent and kings’ heirs, the emperor’s brothers, and the emperor’s sons enfeoffed as commandery kings wear it.

units.zh: 諸王加官者自服其官之冠服，惟太子及王者後常冠焉。
units.en: Princes with extra titles wear those regalia, but heirs and princely successors keep the far-roaming cap daily.
units.literal: For princes who add offices, they themselves wear that office’s cap and robes; only the heir apparent and kings’ heirs regularly wear this cap.

units.zh: 太子則以翠羽為緌，綴以白珠，其餘但青絲而已。
units.en: The crown prince alone may trail kingfisher and pearl tassels; others use plain silk cords.
units.literal: For the heir apparent then kingfisher feathers make the tassel fringe, strung with white pearls; the rest use only blue-green silk.

units.zh: 緇布冠，蔡邕雲即委貌冠也。
units.en: Cai Yong identifies the black cloth cap with the classical weimao.
units.literal: The black cloth cap: Cai Yong says it is the weimao cap.

units.zh: 太古冠布，齊則緇之。
units.en: Ancient caps were undyed cloth until mourners and fasters switched to black.
units.literal: In highest antiquity caps were cloth; for fasting then they blackened them.

units.zh: 緇布冠，始冠之冠也。
units.en: It is the cap placed at a young noble’s first coming-of-age rite.
units.literal: The black cloth cap is the cap of first capping.

units.zh: 其制有四形，一似武冠，又一似進賢，其一上方其下如幘顏，其一刺上而方下。
units.en: Ritualists describe four variants—some like martial caps, some like scholar caps, some squared like a headcloth profile.
units.literal: Its form has four shapes: one resembles the martial cap, another resembles worthy-advancement, one is square above and below like a cap’s brow, one is pointed above and square below.

units.zh: 行鄉射禮則公卿委貌冠，以皁絹為之。
units.en: Community archery required black-silk weimao for high nobles.
units.literal: When performing village archery rite, dukes and ministers wear the weimao cap, made of black silk.

units.zh: 形如覆杯，與皮弁同制，長七寸，高四寸。
units.en: It looks like an upside-down cup, seven by four cun, matching the leather cap mold.
units.literal: The shape is like an inverted cup, same system as the skin cap, seven cun long, four cun high.

units.zh: 衣黑而裳素，其中衣以皁緣領袖。
units.en: Wear black robe, undyed skirt, black-piped under-robe.
units.literal: The robe is black and the skirt plain; the middle garment uses black to border collar and cuffs.

units.zh: 其執事之人皮弁，以鹿皮為之。
units.en: Officiants switch to soft deer-skin bian caps.
units.literal: Those who perform the rites wear skin caps, made of deer skin.

units.zh: 進賢冠，古緇布遺象也，斯蓋文儒者之服。
units.en: The ridged “worthy” cap descends from the black cloth prototype—standard literati headgear.
units.literal: The worthy-advancement cap is the surviving image of ancient black cloth; this is generally scholar dress.

units.zh: 前高七寸，後高三寸，長八寸，有五梁、三梁、二梁、一梁。
units.en: Its profile slopes from seven cun in front to three behind, with one to five horizontal ridges denoting rank.
units.literal: The front is seven cun high, the rear three cun high, eight cun long, having five ridges, three ridges, two ridges, or one ridge.

units.zh: 人主元服，始加緇布，則冠五梁進賢。
units.en: An emperor’s first capping pairs black cloth with the five-ridge scholar cap.
units.literal: When the ruler first caps with the first rites, he first adds black cloth, then caps five-ridge worthy-advancement.

units.zh: 三公及封郡公、縣公、郡侯、縣侯、鄉亭侯，則冠三梁。
units.en: Dukes and marquises of every tier wear three ridges.
units.literal: The three excellencies and enfeoffed commandery dukes, county dukes, commandery marquises, county marquises, and village and pavilion marquises then cap three ridges.

units.zh: 卿、大夫、八座，尚書，關中內侯、二千石及千石以上，則冠兩梁。
units.en: Senior ministers and two-thousand-bushel ranks take two ridges.
units.literal: Ministers, grandees, the eight seats, masters of writing, interior marquises at the passes, two thousand piculs and one thousand piculs and above, then cap two ridges.

units.zh: 中書郎、秘書丞郎、著作郎、尚書丞郎、太子洗馬舍人、六百石以下至於令史、門郎、小史、並冠一梁。
units.en: Mid- and low-level secretaries and clerks wear the single-ridge cap.
units.literal: Secretariat gentlemen, palace library assistants and gentlemen, editorial gentlemen, masters of writing assistants and gentlemen, heir apparent scribes and housemen, six hundred piculs down to record clerks, gate gentlemen, and petty clerks all cap one ridge.

units.zh: 漢建初中，太官令冠兩梁，親省禦膳為重也。
units.en: Even the imperial chef once rated two ridges when tasting the sovereign’s food.
units.literal: In Han’s Jianchu mid-period, the grand provisioner director capped two ridges, because personally inspecting imperial meals was weighty.

units.zh: 博士兩梁，崇儒也。
units.en: Academicians alone merited two ridges to mark learning.
units.literal: Doctors of erudition two ridges, honoring Confucians.

units.zh: 宗室劉氏亦得兩梁冠，示加服也。
units.en: Imperial kinsmen Liu could earn two ridges as a mark of favor.
units.literal: Imperial clan Liu surnames also obtained two-ridge caps, showing added dress.

units.zh: 武冠，一名武弁，一名大冠，一名繁冠，一名建冠，一名籠冠，即古之惠文冠。
units.en: The tall “martial” cap—also called the great cap or cage cap—is the old Huizwen style.
units.literal: The martial cap, one name martial bian, one name great cap, one name many-layer cap, one name founded cap, one name cage cap, is the ancient Huizwen cap.

units.zh: 或曰趙惠文王所造，因以為名。
units.en: Legend credits King Huiwen of Zhao with inventing it.
units.literal: Some say King Huiwen of Zhao created it, therefore took the name.

units.zh: 亦云，惠者蟪也，其冠文輕細如蟬翼，故名惠文。
units.en: Others derive “hui” from “cicada,” noting the gauze weave mimics wings.
units.literal: It is also said “hui” means cicada; the cap’s pattern is light and fine like cicada wings, therefore named Huizwen.

units.zh: 或云，齊人見千歲涸澤之神，名曰慶忌，冠大冠，乘小車，好疾馳，因象其冠而服焉。
units.en: Another tale ties it to the marsh spirit Qingji, who raced in a tall cap.
units.literal: Some say Qi people saw a thousand-year spirit of a dried marsh named Qingji, wearing a great cap, riding a small cart, fond of swift gallop, therefore imitated his cap and wore it.

units.zh: 漢幸臣閎孺為侍中，皆服大冠。
units.en: Han favorites like Hong Ru sported the great cap at court.
units.literal: Han favorite Hong Ru as attendant-in-ordinary all wore the great cap.

units.zh: 天子元服亦先加大冠，左右侍臣及諸將軍武官通服之。
units.en: Emperors began capping with the great cap, as did generals and close attendants.
units.literal: When the Son of Heaven first caps he also first adds the great cap; left and right attendant ministers and various generals and martial officials generally wear it.

units.zh: 侍中、常侍則加金璫，附蟬為飾，插以貂毛，黃金為竿，侍中插左，常侍插右。
units.en: Palace attendants add gold disks, jade cicadas, and sable plumes—left for attendants-in-ordinary, right for regular attendants.
units.literal: For attendant-in-ordinary and regular attendant then add golden dang, attaching cicada as ornament, inserting sable fur, yellow gold as shaft; attendant-in-ordinary inserts left, regular attendant inserts right.

units.zh: 胡廣曰：「昔趙武靈王為胡服，以金貂飾首。
units.en: Hu Guang recalled how Zhao Wuling’s “Hu robes” paired with gilded sable hats.
units.literal: Hu Guang said: “Formerly King Wuling of Zhao made Hu dress, ornamenting the head with gold sable.

units.zh: 秦滅趙，以其君冠賜侍臣。」
units.en: Qin seized Zhao’s royal cap style for palace attendants.”
units.literal: Qin destroyed Zhao and conferred its ruler’s cap on attendant ministers.”

units.zh: 應劭《漢官》云：「說者以為金取剛強，百煉不耗。
units.en: Ying Shao’s Han Offices says: “Expositors hold that gold stands for hardness, refined by fire without loss.
units.literal: Ying Shuo’s Han Offices says: “Expositors take gold as hard, refined by fire without loss.

units.zh: 蟬居高飲清，口在掖下。
units.en: Cicadas “drink dew” aloft—an emblem of purity.
units.literal: The cicada dwells high and drinks purity, its mouth under the armpit.

units.zh: 貂內勁悍而外柔縟。」
units.en: Sable stands for inner strength beneath a supple pelt.”
units.literal: The sable is fierce within yet soft without.”

units.zh: 又以蟬取清高飲露而不食，貂則紫蔚柔潤而毛采不彰灼，金則貴其寶瑩，於義亦有所取。
units.en: Later writers piled meanings: cicadas for abstinent purity, sable for modest brilliance, gold for precious integrity.
units.literal: Moreover because the cicada takes being pure and high, drinking dew and not eating, while the sable is purple luxuriant soft moist and its fur sheen is not glaring, and gold esteems its precious gleam—in meaning each has something taken.

units.zh: 或以為北土多寒，胡人常以貂皮溫額，後世效此，遂以附冠。
units.en: Pragmatists note northern riders wrapped sable across the brow for warmth, which became court fashion.
units.literal: Some think the northern land is very cold; Hu people constantly used sable fur to warm the forehead; later generations imitated this, then attached it to the cap.

units.zh: 漢貂用赤黑色，王莽用黃貂，各附服色所尚也。
units.en: Han favored dark sable; Wang Mang switched to yellow to match his color theory.
units.literal: Han sable used red-black; Wang Mang used yellow sable, each attaching to the dress color honored.

units.zh: 高山冠，一名側注，高九寸，鐵為卷梁，制似通天。
units.en: The “high mountain” or side-tilt cap rises nine cun with an iron roll like tongtian.
units.literal: The high-mountain cap, one name side pour, nine cun high, iron forming the curled beam, system like piercing-heaven.

units.zh: 頂直豎，不斜卻，無山述展筒。
units.en: Unlike tongtian it stands plumb without brow plate or sounding tube.
units.literal: The top stands straight, not slanting backward, without mountain description spreading tube.

units.zh: 高山者，《詩》云「高山仰止」，取其矜莊賓遠者也。
units.en: The name quotes the Odes line “high mountain, look up and stop,” evoking lofty dignity that keeps onlookers at reverent distance.
units.literal: “High mountain” means, the Odes says “high mountain, look up and stop,” taking its dignity and keeping guests far.

units.zh: 中外官、謁者、謁者僕射所服。
units.en: Heralds and court ushers wear this cap.
units.literal: Central and outer officials, ushers, and usher directors wear it.

units.zh: 胡廣曰：「高山，齊王冠也。
units.en: Hu Guang said: “The high-mountain cap was the Qi king’s crown.
units.literal: Hu Guang said: “High mountain is the Qi king’s cap.

units.zh: 傅曰'桓公好高冠大帶'。
units.en: Duke Huan of Qi supposedly loved outsized caps and sashes.
units.literal: The tradition says 'Lord Huan loved tall caps and broad belts.'

units.zh: 秦滅齊，以其君冠賜謁者近臣。」
units.en: Qin gave Qi’s kingly cap to palace heralds.”
units.literal: Qin destroyed Qi and conferred its ruler’s cap on ushers and close ministers.”

units.zh: 應劭曰：「高山，今法冠也，秦行人使官亦服之。」
units.en: Ying Shao equates it with the later “law cap” of Qin envoys.
units.literal: Ying Shuo said: “High mountain is today’s law cap; Qin envoys and traveling officials also wore it.”

units.zh: 而《漢官儀》云「乘輿冠高山之冠，飛翮之纓」，然則天子亦有時服焉。
units.en: Han Offices Protocol says “the imperial carriage caps the high-mountain cap, flying-feather tassels,” so the Son of Heaven also sometimes wore it.
units.literal: And Han Offices Protocol says “the imperial carriage caps the high-mountain cap, flying-feather tassels,” thus the Son of Heaven also sometimes wore it.

units.zh: 《傅子》曰：「魏明帝以其制似通天、遠遊，故改令卑下。」
units.en: Fu Xuan says: “Emperor Ming of Wei, because its form resembled the tongtian and far-roaming caps, therefore ordered it made lower.”
units.literal: The Master Fu says: “Wei Ming Di because its system resembled piercing-heaven and far-roaming, therefore ordered it made lower.”

units.zh: 法冠，一名柱後，或謂之獬豸冠。
units.en: The “law cap,” or pillar-back hat, is the unicorn-judge style.
units.literal: The law cap, one name pillar rear, some call it the xiezhi cap.

units.zh: 高五寸，以縰為展筒。
units.en: It stands five cun with a gauze “sounding” tube.
units.literal: Five cun high, using fine cloth for spreading tube.

units.zh: 鐵為柱卷，取其不曲撓也。
units.en: Iron stiffeners symbolize unbending justice.
units.literal: Iron makes the pillar curl, taking its not bending.

units.zh: 侍御史、廷尉正監平，凡執法官皆服之。
units.en: Censors and court inspectors wear it as their badge.
units.literal: Attending censors, commandant of justice rectifiers and overseers, in general all law officials wear it.

units.zh: 或謂獬豸神羊，能觸邪佞。
units.en: Myth calls the xiezhi a one-horn ram that gores the unjust.
units.literal: Some say the xiezhi is a divine ram able to strike the crooked and flattering.

units.zh: 《異物志》云：「北荒之中，有獸名獬豸，一角，性別曲直。
units.en: The Record of Strange Creatures says: “In the northern wilds there is a beast named xiezhi, one horn, nature distinguishing crooked and straight.
units.literal: The Record of Strange Creatures says: “In the northern wilds there is a beast named xiezhi, one horn, nature distinguishing crooked and straight.

units.zh: 見人鬥，觸不直者。
units.en: In brawls it butts the guilty party.
units.literal: Seeing people fight, it gores the not straight.

units.zh: 聞人爭，咋不正者。
units.en: In quarrels it snaps at the liar.
units.literal: Hearing people quarrel, it bites the not correct.

units.zh: 楚王嘗獲此獸，因象其形以制衣冠。」
units.en: A king of Chu supposedly modeled court dress on the creature.”
units.literal: The king of Chu once captured this beast, then modeled its form to make cap and robe.”

units.zh: 胡廣曰：「《春秋左氏傳》晉侯觀於軍府，見鐘儀，曰'南冠而縶者誰也'？
units.en: Hu Guang links it to the “southern cap” prisoner in Zuo’s Commentary.
units.literal: Hu Guang said: “In Zuo’s Spring and Autumn Commentary the marquis of Jin inspected the army storehouse, saw Zhong Yi, and said ‘The southern cap and bound one—who is he?’

units.zh: 南冠即楚冠。
units.en: That “southern cap” meant Chu headgear.
units.literal: The southern cap is the Chu cap.

units.zh: 秦滅楚，以其冠服賜執法臣也。」
units.en: Qin destroyed Chu and conferred its cap and robe on law-executing ministers.”
units.literal: Qin destroyed Chu and conferred its cap and robe on law-executing ministers.”

units.zh: 長冠，一名齊冠。
units.en: The “long cap” is also called the Qi-style crown.
units.literal: The long cap, one name Qi cap.

units.zh: 高七寸，廣三寸，漆纚為之，制如版，以竹為裏。
units.en: Seven by three cun, board-shaped, built on a bamboo frame with lacquered mesh.
units.literal: Seven cun high, three cun wide, lacquered gauze makes it; the system is like a board, bamboo as inner frame.

units.zh: 漢高祖微時，以竹皮為此冠，其世因謂劉氏冠。
units.en: Liu Bang invented a bamboo-skin version later nicknamed the Liu family cap.
units.literal: When Han Gaozu was lowly, he used bamboo skin for this cap; his age therefore called it the Liu clan cap.

units.zh: 後除竹用漆纚。
units.en: Later makers replaced bamboo with lacquer-soaked silk.
units.literal: Afterward they removed bamboo and used lacquered gauze.

units.zh: 司馬彪曰：「長冠蓋楚制。
units.en: Sima Biao said: “The long cap is probably a Chu institution.
units.literal: Sima Biao said: “The long cap is probably Chu system.

units.zh: 人間或謂之鵲尾冠，非也。
units.en: Folk wrongly call it a “magpie tail.”
units.literal: People sometimes call it the magpie-tail cap; that is not correct.

units.zh: 救日蝕則服長冠，而祠宗廟諸祀冠之。
units.en: Astronomers wore it for eclipse rites; it became temple dress.
units.literal: When rescuing solar eclipse they wear the long cap, and for sacrificing to the ancestral temple various sacrifices they cap it.

units.zh: 此高祖所造，後世以為祭服，尊敬之至也。」
units.en: This is what Gaozu created; later generations took it as sacrificial dress, utmost veneration.”
units.literal: This is what Gaozu created; later generations took it as sacrificial dress, utmost veneration.”

units.zh: 建華冠，以鐵為柱卷，貫大銅珠九枚，古用雜木珠，原憲所冠華冠是也。
units.en: The ritual “splendor” cap threads nine bronze beads on iron—Yuan Xian’s tall cap was this type.
units.literal: The splendor-blossom cap uses iron for pillar curl, piercing nine great copper beads; antiquity used mixed wood beads; what Yuan Xian capped as splendor cap is this.

units.zh: 又《春秋左氏傳》鄭子臧好聚鷸冠，謂建華是也。
units.en: Zuo tells of Zheng prince Zang’s kingfisher “splendor” cap—same family.
units.literal: Moreover Zuo’s Spring and Autumn Commentary: Zang of Zheng loved gathering kingfisher caps, called splendor-blossom is this.

units.zh: 祀天地、五郊、明堂，舞人服之。
units.en: Altar dancers still wear it for heaven, earth, five directions, and hall rites.
units.literal: For sacrificing to heaven and earth, five suburbs, and bright hall, dancers wear it.

units.zh: 漢《育命舞》樂人所服。
units.en: Han “Nurture Destiny” musicians used it.
units.literal: Han Nurture Destiny dancers wore it.

units.zh: 方山冠，其制似進賢。
units.en: The square-mountain cap copies the scholar-cap profile.
units.literal: The square-mountain cap, its system resembles worthy-advancement.

units.zh: 鄭展曰：「方山冠，以五采縠為之。」
units.en: Zheng Zhan said: “The square-mountain cap uses five-color gauze to make it.”
units.literal: Zheng Zhan said: “The square-mountain cap uses five-color gauze to make it.”

units.zh: 漢《大予》、《八佾》、《五行》樂人所服，冠衣各如其行方之色而舞焉。
units.en: Grand Music performers matched cap colors to the five directions.
units.literal: Han Grand Music, eight rows, and Five Agents musicians wore it; cap and robe each matched their row’s color direction and danced.

units.zh: 巧士冠，前高七寸，要後相通，直豎。
units.en: The “clever gentleman” cap is a tall straight front-to-back piece.
units.literal: The clever-gentleman cap, seven cun high in front, the waist and rear connecting, standing straight.

units.zh: 此冠不常用，漢氏惟郊天，黃門從官四人冠之；
units.en: Han emperors used it rarely—four yellow-gate runners at suburban heaven rites.
units.literal: This cap is not commonly used; Han only at suburban heaven, four yellow-gate followers capped it;

units.zh: 在鹵簿中，夾乘輿車前，以備宦者四星。
units.en: They flanked the chariot to symbolize the four “eunuch” constellations.
units.literal: Within the escort, flanking the imperial carriage front, to supply the four eunuch stars.

units.zh: 或云，掃除從官所服。
units.en: Others say it marked sweepers in train.
units.literal: Some say it is what sweepers and followers wear.

units.zh: 卻非冠，高五寸，制似長冠。
units.en: The five-inch “reject wrong” cap resembles the long cap.
units.literal: The “reject wrong” cap, five cun high, system like long cap.

units.zh: 宮殿門吏僕射冠之。
units.en: Palace gatekeepers wear it.
units.literal: Palace gate clerks and gate directors cap it.

units.zh: 負赤幡，青翅燕尾，諸僕射幡皆如之。
units.en: They carry red swallow-tailed banners like other gate officers.
units.literal: They bear red banners, green wings swallow-tail; the various directors’ banners are all like this.

units.zh: 卻敵冠，前高四寸，通長四寸，後高三寸，制似進賢。
units.en: The “repel foe” cap is a compact scholar-cap profile for guards.
units.literal: The “repel enemy” cap, four cun high in front, four cun total length, three cun high in rear, system like worthy-advancement.

units.zh: 凡當殿門衛士服之。
units.en: Hall sentinels at palace doors use it.
units.literal: In general hall gate guards wear it.

units.zh: 樊噲冠，廣九寸，高七寸，前後出各四寸，制似平冕。
units.en: Fan Kuai’s cap is nine by seven cun with four-cun brims, shaped like the flat sacrificial crown.
units.literal: The Fan Kuai cap, nine cun wide, seven cun high, front and rear each protruding four cun, system like level crown.

units.zh: 昔楚漢會於鴻門，項籍圖危高祖，樊噲常持鐵楯，聞急，乃裂裳苞楯，戴以為冠，排入羽營，因數羽罪，漢王乘間得出。
units.en: At Hongmen Fan Kuai ripped his skirt, wrapped his shield as a makeshift cap, burst into Xiang Yu’s camp, and berated him until Liu Bang slipped away.
units.literal: Formerly Chu and Han met at Hongmen; Xiang Yu plotted danger to the High Ancestor; Fan Kuai always held an iron shield; hearing urgency, then tore skirt wrapping the shield, wore it as cap, pushed into the feather camp, then enumerated Yu’s crimes; the king of Han took the gap and escaped.

units.zh: 後人壯其意，乃制冠象焉。
units.en: Later generations immortalized the gesture in a formal cap.
units.literal: Later people admired his intent, then made a cap imitating it.

units.zh: 凡殿門司馬衛士服之。
units.en: Palace gate marshals wear the Fan Kuai style.
units.literal: In general hall gate marshals and guards wear it.

units.zh: 術氏冠，前圓，吳制，差池四重。
units.en: The round-front Wu-style “Shu” cap stacks four tiers.
units.literal: The Shu clan cap, round in front, Wu system, staggered four layers.

units.zh: 趙武靈王好服之。
units.en: Zhao Wuling favored it.
units.literal: King Wuling of Zhao liked to wear it.

units.zh: 或曰，楚莊王復仇冠是也。
units.en: Others link it to King Zhuang of Chu’s “vengeance” crown.
units.literal: Some say it is the Chu Zhuang king revenge cap.

units.zh: 鶡冠，加雙鶡尾，豎插兩邊。
units.en: The he warrior cap mounts twin pheasant tails upright.
units.literal: The he cap adds double he tail feathers, vertically inserted on two sides.

units.zh: 鶡，鳥名也，形類鷂而微黑，性果勇，其鬥到死乃止。
units.en: The he is a fierce blackish hawk that fights to the death.
units.literal: He is a bird name; its form resembles a goshawk but slightly black; its nature is indeed brave; its fights until death then stop.

units.zh: 上党貢之，趙武靈王以表顯壯士。
units.en: Shangdang sent the feathers; Zhao Wuling awarded them to champions.
units.literal: Shangdang presented them; King Wuling of Zhao used them to display brave men.

units.zh: 至秦漢，猶施之武人。
units.en: Qin and Han warriors still wore he plumes.
units.literal: Down to Qin and Han, they still applied them to martial men.

units.zh: 皮弁，以鹿皮淺毛黃白色者為之。
units.en: The bian cap uses pale yellow deerskin.
units.literal: The skin bian uses deer skin with shallow fur yellow-white to make it.

units.zh: 《禮》「王皮弁，會五采玉，象邸玉笄」，謂之合皮為弁。
units.en: The Rites: “The king’s skin bian joins five-color jade, elephant-foot jade hairpins,” called joining skins to make the bian.
units.literal: The Rites: “The king’s skin bian joins five-color jade, elephant foot-stool jade hairpin,” called joining skins to make bian.

units.zh: 其縫中名曰會，以采玉硃為，
units.en: The crown seam junction is called the hui, inlaid with colored jade.
units.literal: Its seam middle is called hui, using colored jade and vermilion to make,

units.zh: 結也。
units.en: The following gloss reads “fastened,” explaining the hairpin’s knot.
units.literal: meaning “to knot.”

units.zh: 天子五采，諸侯三采。
units.en: Emperors use five jade hues; lords three.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven five colors; feudal lords three colors.

units.zh: 邸，冠下抵也，象骨為之，音帝也。
units.en: The “di” block under the cap is carved ivory, homophone to “emperor.”
units.literal: Di means the cap’s lower rest; elephant bone makes it, pronounced like di.

units.zh: 天子則縫十二，公侯伯七，子男五，孤四，卿大夫三。
units.en: Seam counts mark rank—twelve for the throne down to three for ministers.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven then has twelve seams; dukes, marquises, and earls seven; viscounts and barons five; solitary four; ministers and grandees three.

units.zh: 韋弁，制似皮弁，頂上尖，韎草染之，色如淺絳。
units.en: The leather bian resembles the deer cap but peaks sharper, dyed pink-crimson with wei herb.
units.literal: The leather bian, system like skin bian, pointed on top, dyed with wei grass, color like light crimson.

units.zh: 爵弁，一名廣冕。
units.en: The “duke” bian is also called the broad sacrificial crown.
units.literal: The duke bian, one name wide mian.

units.zh: 高八寸，長尺二寸，如爵形，前小後大。
units.en: It stands eight cun, spans a foot two, shaped like a ritual jue cup—narrow in front, broad behind.
units.literal: Eight cun high, one chi two cun long, like a duke-vessel shape, small in front, large in rear.

units.zh: 增其上似爵頭色。
units.en: The crown mimics the flared lip of a bronze jue.
units.literal: They enlarge the upper part like a jue head color.

units.zh: 有收持笄，所謂夏收殷哻者也。
units.en: It keeps the ancient hairpin loops associated with Xia and Shang court caps.
units.literal: It keeps the ancient hairpin loops associated with Xia and Shang court caps.

units.zh: 祠天地、五郊、明堂，《雲翹舞》樂人服之。
units.en: Altar dancers in the “Cloud Wing” suite wear this crown.
units.literal: For sacrificing to heaven and earth, five suburbs, and bright hall, Cloud Wing dancers wear it.

units.zh: 幘者，古賤人不冠者之服也。
units.en: The ze was originally headwrap for commoners barred from formal caps.
units.literal: The headcloth is what ancient lowly people who did not cap wore.

units.zh: 漢元帝額有壯發，始引幘服之。
units.en: Emperor Yuan of Han hid a prominent hairline with a ze wrap, starting a fad.
units.literal: Han Yuandi had a strong hairline on the forehead, then first drew the headcloth and wore it.

units.zh: 王莽頂禿，又加其屋也。
units.en: Wang Mang stacked a higher roof to cover his bald crown.
units.literal: Wang Mang was bald on top, again added its roof.

units.zh: 《漢注》曰，冠進賢者宜長耳，今介幘也。
units.en: Han notes pair long “ears” with scholar caps—ancestors of the stiff court ze.
units.literal: Han Commentary says, those who cap worthy-advancement should have long ears; today’s stiff cap.

units.zh: 冠惠文者宜短耳，今平上幘也。
units.en: Martial Huizwen caps use short ears—the level-top ze line.
units.literal: Those who cap Huizwen should have short ears; today’s level-top ze.

units.zh: 始時各隨所宜，遂因冠為別。
units.en: Styles diverged until cap type dictated ze shape.
units.literal: At first each followed what was fitting, then followed the cap to make distinction.

units.zh: 介幘服文吏，平上幘服武官也。
units.en: Civil versus military headwraps became fixed.
units.literal: Stiff caps dress civil clerks; level-top ze dress martial officials.

units.zh: 童子幘無屋者，示不成人也。
units.en: Boys wear roofless zes until capping.
units.literal: Children’s ze without roof shows not yet adult.

units.zh: 又有納言幘，幘後收又一重，方三寸。
units.en: Palace “inner edict” zes add a triple-cun rear fold.
units.literal: Moreover there is the “inner edict” ze, the ze rear gathered again one layer, square three cun.

units.zh: 又有赤幘，騎吏、武吏、乘輿鼓吹所服。
units.en: Red zes mark outriders, guards, and imperial bands.
units.literal: Moreover there is the red ze, worn by mounted clerks, martial clerks, and imperial musicians.

units.zh: 救日蝕，文武官皆免冠著幘，對朝服，示武威也。
units.en: During eclipse rites everyone doffed caps for red zes over court robes as a martial gesture.
units.literal: When rescuing solar eclipse, civil and martial officials all remove caps and wear zes, facing court dress, showing martial awe.

units.zh: 漢儀，立秋日獵，服緗幘。
units.en: Han autumn hunts required buff-colored zes.
units.literal: Han ritual: on Liqiu hunt day they wore light-yellow zes.

units.zh: 及江左，哀帝從博士曹弘之等議，立秋禦讀令，改用素白㡊。
units.en: Eastern Jin Ai Di switched Liqiu court dress to plain white scarves per scholars’ advice.
units.literal: When it came to Jiangzuo, Emperor Ai followed doctors Cao Hongzhi and others’ proposal: for the Liqiu imperial edict ceremony they changed to plain white kerchiefs.

units.zh: 案漢末王公名士多委王服，以幅巾為雅，是以袁紹、崔鈞之徒，雖為將帥，皆著縑巾。
units.en: Late Han elites favored simple headcloths—even generals like Yuan Shao wore plain silk wraps.
units.literal: According to investigation, late Han kings, dukes, and famous gentlemen mostly cast off kingly dress, taking plain headcloth as elegant; therefore Yuan Shao, Cui Jun and the like, although generals, all wore thin-silk headcloths.

units.zh: 魏武以天下凶荒，資財乏匱，擬古皮弁，裁縑帛以為㡊，合乎簡易隨時之義，以色別其貴賤，本施軍飾，非為國容也。
units.en: Cao Cao issued colored silk “kerchief-caps” during famine to simplify military dress, not formal regalia.
units.literal: Wei Wu because the realm was violent and famine, goods and wealth exhausted, modeled ancient skin bian, cutting silk to make kerchief, matching simple ease suiting the times’ meaning, using color to distinguish noble and base; originally applied as military dress, not as state appearance.

units.zh: 徐爰曰：「俗說㡊本未有岐，荀文若巾之行，觸樹枝成岐，謂之為善，因而弗改。」
units.en: Xu Ai tells how Xun Yu’s kerchief snagged into lucky forked tails that became fashion.”
units.literal: Xu Ai said: “Popular story says the kerchief originally had no fork; when Xun Wenruo’s kerchief walked, it touched a tree branch forming a fork; they called it auspicious, therefore did not change.”

units.zh: 今通以為慶吊服。
units.en: Later society adopted forked kerchiefs for both joyous and funerary wear.
units.literal: Now it is generally taken as congratulation and mourning dress.

units.zh: 巾，以葛為之，形如㡊而橫著之，古尊卑共服也。
units.en: Ge-cloth scarves, worn sideways like caps, were once universal.
units.literal: The headcloth uses kudzu to make it; the shape is like a kerchief but worn horizontally; ancient noble and base together wore it.

units.zh: 故漢末妖賊以黃為巾，世謂黃巾賊。
units.en: Hence the Yellow Turbans took their name from saffron scarves.
units.literal: Therefore late Han rebel bandits used yellow as headcloth; the age called them Yellow Turban bandits.

units.zh: 帽名猶冠也，義取于蒙覆其首，其本纚也。
units.en: “Hat” functionally replaced “crown,” evolving from hair mesh.
units.literal: The hat’s name is still “crown”; the meaning takes from covering the head; its origin is the fine mesh wrap.

units.zh: 古者冠無幘，冠下有纚，以繒為之。
units.en: Early crowns used silk hairnets instead of zes.
units.literal: In antiquity crowns had no ze; below the crown there was li, made of silk.

units.zh: 後世施幘於冠，因或裁纓為帽。
units.en: Later courts fused ze with crown and tailored brimmed hats.
units.literal: Later generations applied ze to crowns, then sometimes cut tassels into hats.

units.zh: 自乘輿宴居，下至庶人無爵者皆服之。
units.en: Everyone from the emperor at leisure to commoners wears soft hats.
units.literal: From the imperial carriage at leisure down to commoners without rank all wear them.

units.zh: 成帝咸和九年，制聽尚書八座丞郎、門下三省侍官乘車，白㡊低幃，出入掖門。
units.en: Xianhe nine let senior clerks ride through side gates in white scarves and low screens.
units.literal: In Emperor Cheng’s ninth Xianhe year, regulation allowed masters of writing eight seats assistants and gentlemen, gate and three departments attendant officials, to ride carts, white kerchief low curtain, entering and leaving the side palace gates.

units.zh: 又，二宮直官著烏紗㡊。
units.en: Palace watch officers don black gauze caps.
units.literal: Moreover, two-palace duty officials wear black gauze kerchiefs.

units.zh: 然則往往士人宴居皆著㡊矣。
units.en: Soon every scholar lounged in kerchief caps.
units.literal: Thus commonly gentlemen at leisure all wore kerchiefs.

units.zh: 而江左時野人已著帽，人士亦往往而然，但其頂圓耳，後乃高其屋雲。
units.en: Southerners borrowed peasants’ round hats, then heightened the crown for fashion.
units.literal: Yet in Jiangzuo times rustics already wore hats; gentlemen also often did so, but their tops were round; afterward they raised the roof, it is said.

units.zh: 漢制，自天子至於百官，無不佩劍，其後惟朝帶劍。
units.en: Han once required swords for all ranks; later only court audiences kept the habit.
units.literal: Han institutions: from the Son of Heaven down to the hundred officials, none did not wear swords; afterward only at court did they belt swords.

units.zh: 晉世始代之以木，貴者猶用玉首，賤者亦用蚌、金銀、玳瑁為雕飾。
units.en: Jin switched to wooden blades with jade or shell hilts by rank.
units.literal: The Jin age first replaced them with wood; the noble still used jade heads; the base also used mussel, gold, silver, and tortoiseshell for carved ornament.

units.zh: 乘輿六璽，秦制也。
units.en: Six imperial jades follow Qin precedent.
units.literal: The imperial carriage six seals is Qin system.

units.zh: 曰「皇帝行璽」、「皇帝之璽」、「皇帝信璽」、「天子行璽」、「天子之璽」、「天子信璽」，漢遵秦不改。
units.en: The six mottoes—three for “emperor,” three for “Son of Heaven”—survived unchanged from Qin into Han.
units.literal: They are called “Emperor traveling seal,” “Emperor’s seal,” “Emperor trust seal,” “Heavenly Son traveling seal,” “Heavenly Son’s seal,” “Heavenly Son trust seal”; Han followed Qin without change.

units.zh: 又有秦始皇藍田玉璽，螭獸紐，在六璽之外，文曰「受天之命，皇帝壽昌」。
units.en: Beyond the six sits the Lantian jade heirloom with horned-dragon knob; the inscription reads “Receiving heaven’s mandate, the emperor long prosperous.”
units.literal: Moreover there is the First Emperor of Qin’s Lantian jade seal, chi-beast knob, outside the six seals; the inscription reads “Receiving heaven’s mandate, the emperor long prosperous.”

units.zh: 漢高祖佩之，後世名曰傳國璽，與斬白蛇劍俱為乘輿所寶。
units.en: Liu Bang claimed both the “transmission seal” and the snake sword as regalia.
units.literal: Han Gaozu wore it; later generations named it the transmission-of-state seal, together with the white-snake-slaying sword treasured by the imperial carriage.

units.zh: 斬白蛇劍至惠帝時武庫火燒之，遂亡。
units.en: The fabled sword burned in the armory fire in the time of Emperor Hui (Jin), and was lost.
units.literal: The white-snake-slaying sword reached Emperor Hui when the armory fire burned it, then was lost.

units.zh: 及懷帝沒胡，傳國璽沒于劉聰，後又沒于石勒。
units.en: The seal passed from Jin captivity to Liu Cong, then Shi Le.
units.literal: When Emperor Huai fell to the Hu, the transmission seal was lost to Liu Cong, afterward again lost to Shi Le.

units.zh: 及石季龍死，胡亂，穆帝世乃還江南。
units.en: It resurfaced in the south only after Shi Hu’s death and turmoil.
units.literal: When Shi Jilong died, Hu chaos; in Emperor Mu’s age it then returned south of the Yangzi.

units.zh: 革帶，古之鞶帶也，謂之鞶革，文武眾官牧守丞令下及騶寺皆服之。
units.en: The leather “pan” belt girds everyone from magistrates to outriders.
units.literal: The leather belt is the ancient pan belt, called pan leather; civil and martial multitude of officials, shepherds, guards, magistrates down to outriders and temple attendants all wear it.

units.zh: 其有囊綬，則以綴於革帶，其戎服則以皮絡帶代之。
units.en: Civil belts carry purple sash bags; field dress swaps in leather mesh.
units.literal: If there is sash pouch, then attach it to the leather belt; for martial dress then substitute leather net belts.

units.zh: 八坐尚書荷紫，以生紫為袷囊，綴之服外，加于左肩。
units.en: Senior ministers wear purple document pouches slung from the left shoulder.
units.literal: The eight seats masters of writing bear purple, using raw purple for lapel pouch, attaching it outside the robe on the left shoulder.

units.zh: 昔周公負成王，制此服衣，至今以為朝服。
units.en: Myth credits the Zhou regent’s baby-carrying sash for today’s court pouch.
units.literal: Formerly the Duke of Zhou carried King Cheng on his back, making this robe; down to today it is taken as court dress.

units.zh: 或云漢世用盛奏事，負之以行，未詳也。
units.en: Others say Han clerks slung memorial tubes there—uncertain.
units.literal: Some say Han generations used it to hold memorials, carrying them on the back; not detailed.

units.zh: 車前五百者，卿行旅從，五百人為一旅。
units.en: “Five hundred front” recalled a full brigade escorting ministers.
units.literal: The five hundred before the chariot: ministers’ processions follow, five hundred men make one brigade.

units.zh: 漢氏一統，故去其人，留其名也。
units.en: Han kept the title after disbanding the real five-hundred guard.
units.literal: The Han house unified the realm, therefore removed the men but kept the name.

units.zh: 袴褶之制，未詳所起，近世凡車駕親戎、中外戒嚴服之。
units.en: Military tunics and riding breeches appear for imperial campaigns and palace alerts.
units.literal: The trousers-and-jacket system’s origin is not detailed; in recent generations whenever the chariot personally campaigns inside and outside alert they wear it.

units.zh: 服無定色，冠黑帽，綴紫摽，摽以繒為之，長四寸，廣一寸，腰有絡帶以代鞶。
units.en: Alert dress uses black hats with purple silk markers and mesh waistbands.
units.literal: Dress has no fixed color; cap black hat, attaching purple streamer tag; the tag is made of silk, four cun long, one cun wide; the waist has net belt replacing pan.

units.zh: 中官紫摽，外官絳摽。
units.en: Palace staff wear purple tabs; field officers crimson.
units.literal: Inner officials purple tags; outer officials crimson tags.

units.zh: 又有纂嚴戎服而不綴摽，行留文武悉同。
units.en: Full mobilization dress drops the streamer tags but otherwise matches.
units.literal: Moreover there is assembled strict martial dress without attaching tags; stationary and traveling civil and martial are all the same.

units.zh: 其畋獵巡幸，則惟從官戎服帶鞶革，文官不下纓，武官脫冠。
units.en: On hunts, civil aides keep tassels up while soldiers shed formal caps.
units.literal: For hunting and touring, then only followers wear martial dress with pan leather belts; civil officials do not lower tassels; martial officials remove caps.

units.zh: 漢制，一歲五郊，天子與執事者所服各如方色，百官不執事者服常服絳衣以從。
units.en: Han suburban rounds color-coded officiants while others wore plain crimson.
units.literal: Han institutions: one year five suburbs; the Son of Heaven and those who officiate wear colors matching each direction; the hundred officials who do not officiate wear regular dress crimson robes to follow.

units.zh: 魏秘書監秦靜曰：「漢氏承秦，改六冕之制，但玄冠絳衣而已。」
units.en: Qin Jing noted Han simplified Zhou’s six crowns to black cap and red robe.”
units.literal: Wei palace library director Qin Jing said: “Han inherited Qin, changed the six-crown system, only black cap and crimson robe.”

units.zh: 魏已來名為五時朝服，又有四時朝服，又有朝服。
units.en: Wei–Jin codified “five-season” and “four-season” court wardrobes.
units.literal: From Wei onward it was named five-season court dress; moreover there was four-season court dress; moreover there was court dress.

units.zh: 自皇太子以下隨官受給。
units.en: Ranks down to the heir draw costumes by appointment.
units.literal: From the crown prince downward, each follows office to receive issue.

units.zh: 百官雖服五時朝服，據今止給四時朝服，闕秋服。
units.en: Jin budgets skipped autumn palettes despite five-season theory.
units.literal: Although the hundred officials wear five-season court dress, according to present practice they only issue four-season court dress, lacking autumn dress.

units.zh: 三年一易。
units.en: Sets renew triennially.
units.literal: Every three years one change.

units.zh: 諸假印綬而官不給鞶囊者，得自具作，其但假印不假綬者，不得佩綬鞶，古制也。
units.en: Acting officials without formal sashes may not wear ribbon belts.
units.literal: For those lent seals and ribbons but offices do not issue pan pouches, they may make them themselves; for those only lent seals but not ribbons, they may not wear ribbon pan—ancient system.

units.zh: 漢世著鞶囊者，側在腰間，或謂之傍囊，或謂之綬囊，然則以紫囊盛綬也。
units.en: Han hung purple “side pouches” for credential tubes.
units.literal: For Han generations those wearing pan pouches placed them at the waist side; some called them side pouches, some called them ribbon pouches; thus they used purple pouches to hold ribbons.

units.zh: 或盛或散，各有其時。
units.en: Full or empty pouches followed seasonal rules.
units.literal: Sometimes full sometimes scattered, each has its season.

units.zh: 笏，古者貴賤皆執笏，其有事則搢之於腰帶，所謂搢紳之士者，搢笏而垂紳帶也。
units.en: All ranks once carried hu tablets tucked in sashes—“gentry” literally meant tablet and sash.
units.literal: The tablet: in antiquity noble and base all held tablets; when there was business then they tucked them in the waist belt—what is called “tablet-girdle gentlemen” is tucking tablet while hanging sash belt.

units.zh: 紳垂長三尺。
units.en: Ceremonial sashes trail three chi.
units.literal: The sash hangs three chi long.

units.zh: 笏者，有事則書之，故常簪筆，今之白筆是其遺象。
units.en: Tablets doubled as note boards—hence the white brush pin survives.
units.literal: The tablet: when there was business then they wrote on it, therefore constantly pinned brush; today’s white brush is its surviving image.

units.zh: 三台五省二品文官簪之，王、公、侯、伯、子、男、卿尹及武官不簪，加內侍位者乃簪之。
units.en: Only high civil bureaus and inner-court add-ons wear brush pins.
units.literal: Three terraces five departments second-rank civil officials pin them; kings, dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, barons, ministers and prefects and martial officials do not pin; only those who add inner attendant posts pin them.

units.zh: 手版即古笏矣。
units.en: The board-shaped hu is the old tablet.
units.literal: The hand tablet is the ancient hu.

units.zh: 尚書令、僕射、尚書手版頭復有白筆，以紫皮裹之，名曰笏。
units.en: Ministers of state cap their hu with purple-sheathed white brushes.
units.literal: Masters of writing director, vice, masters of writing have white brush atop the hand tablet, wrapped in purple leather, called hu.

units.zh: 皇太子金璽龜鈕，硃黃綬，四采：赤、黃、縹、紺。
units.en: The crown prince wears gold tortoise seal and four-hued sash.
units.literal: The heir apparent’s gold seal tortoise knob, cinnabar-yellow sash, four colors: red, yellow, light blue, dark blue.

units.zh: 給五時朝服、遠遊冠，介幘、翠緌。
units.en: He receives five-season wardrobe, far-roaming cap, stiff ze, kingfisher fringe.
units.literal: Issued five-season court dress, far-roaming cap, stiff cap, kingfisher tassel.

units.zh: 佩瑜玉，垂組。
units.en: He wears flawless jade pendants on silk cords.
units.literal: Wearing fine jade, hanging cords.

units.zh: 硃衣絳紗襮，皁緣白紗，其中衣白曲領。
units.en: Scarlet court robe over white gauze with black piping and curved collar.
units.literal: Cinnabar robe crimson gauze half-arm, black-bordered white gauze, middle garment white curved collar.

units.zh: 帶劍，火珠素首。
units.en: He belts a sword with plain hilt and “fire pearl” ornament.
units.literal: Bearing sword, fire pearl plain hilt.

units.zh: 革帶，玉鉤燮獸頭鞶囊。
units.en: His belt uses jade hooks and beast-head pouch.
units.literal: Leather belt, jade hook tile beast-head pan pouch.

units.zh: 其大小會、祠宗廟、朔望、五日還朝皆朝服，常還上宮則硃服，預上宮正會則于殿下脫劍舄。
units.en: He changes between full court, palace crimson, and disarmed hall dress by occasion.
units.literal: For great and small assemblies, sacrificing to the ancestral temple, new and full moons, fifth-day returns to court, all court dress; regularly returning to the upper palace then cinnabar dress; when attending upper palace great session then below the hall remove sword and shoes.

units.zh: 又有三梁進賢冠。
units.en: He also owns the three-ridge scholar cap.
units.literal: Moreover there is three-ridge worthy-advancement cap.

units.zh: 其侍祀則平冕九旒，袞衣九章，白紗絳緣中單，絳繒韠，采畫織成袞帶，金辟邪首，紫綠二色帶，采畫廣領、曲領各一，赤舄絳襪。
units.en: Sacrifice calls for nine-tasseled flat crown, nine-dragon robe, layered sashes, and red footgear.
units.literal: When attending sacrifice then level crown nine tassels, nine-emblem sacrificial robe, white gauze crimson-bordered inner robe, crimson silk knee covers, woven five-color sacrificial belt, golden bixie beast head, purple and green two-color belt, painted broad collar and curved collar one each, red shoes crimson socks.

units.zh: 若講，則著介幘單衣。
units.en: For lectures he dons simple ze and robe.
units.literal: If lecturing, then wear stiff cap unlined robe.

units.zh: 釋奠，則遠遊冠，玄朝服，絳緣中單，絳袴襪，玄舄。
units.en: Confucian rites use far-roaming cap and black ensemble.
units.literal: For school sacrifice to the former sage, then far-roaming cap, black court dress, crimson-bordered inner robe, crimson trousers and socks, black shoes.

units.zh: 若未加元服，則中舍人執冕從，介幘單衣玄服。
units.en: Uncapped princes follow with an attendant carrying the mian crown while they wear black ze robes.
units.literal: If he has not yet added the capping, then the household aide holds the crown following, stiff cap unlined robe black dress.

units.zh: 諸王金璽龜鈕，纁硃綬，四采：硃、黃、縹、紺。
units.en: Princes of the blood wear gold tortoise seals and four-color sashes.
units.literal: Princes’ gold seal tortoise knob, reddish-cinnabar sash, four colors: cinnabar, yellow, light blue, dark blue.

units.zh: 五時朝服，遠遊冠介幘，亦有三梁進賢冠。
units.en: They mirror the heir’s wardrobe minus certain honors.
units.literal: Five-season court dress, far-roaming cap stiff cap, also having three-ridge worthy-advancement cap.

units.zh: 硃衣絳紗襮皁緣，中衣表素。
units.en: Their court coat pairs scarlet panels with plain underlayers.
units.literal: Cinnabar robe crimson gauze half-arm black border, middle garment surface plain.

units.zh: 革帶，黑舄，佩山玄玉，垂組，大帶。
units.en: Black shoes, mountain-dark jade, and broad sash complete the look.
units.literal: Leather belt, black shoes, wearing mountain-dark jade, hanging cords, great sash.

units.zh: 若加餘官，則服其加官之服也。
units.en: Extra titles bring matching uniforms.
units.literal: If additional offices are added, then wear the added office’s dress.

units.zh: 皇后謁廟，其服皁上皁下，親蠶則青上縹下，皆深衣制，隱領，袖緣以絛。
units.en: The empress wears deep black for temples, green-blue for silkworm, piped deep robes.
units.literal: When the empress visits the temple, her dress is black above and black below; for personal silkworm then green above and light blue below; all deep-robe system, hidden collar, cuffs bordered with tape.

units.zh: 首飾則假髻，步搖，俗謂之珠松是也，簪珥。
units.en: Her hair uses false chignons, buyao tremblers, pins, and earrings.
units.literal: For head ornaments then false topknot, buyao, vulgarly called pearl pine is this, hairpins and earrings.

units.zh: 步搖以黃金為山題，貫白珠為支相繆。
units.en: Buyao frames are golden “mountains” strung with white pearls.
units.literal: The buyao uses gold for mountain title, piercing white pearls as branches intertwining.

units.zh: 八爵九華，熊、獸、赤羆、天鹿、辟邪、南山豐大特六獸，諸爵獸皆以翡翠為毛羽，金題白珠榼，繞以翡翠為華。
units.en: The crown bristles with jeweled birds and beasts—sparrows, bears, deer, exorcist lions—all feathered in kingfisher and gold.
units.literal: Eight sparrows nine blossoms, bear, beast, red bear, heavenly deer, bixie, southern mountain great boar six beasts; the various sparrow beasts all use kingfisher for feathers and fur, gold title white pearl cups, wound with kingfisher for blossoms.

units.zh: 元康六年，詔曰：「魏以來皇后蠶服皆以文繡，非古義也。
units.en: In the sixth year of Yuankang, an edict said: “Since Wei, empresses’ silkworm dress has all used patterned embroidery; it is not ancient meaning.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Yuankang, an edict said: “Since Wei, empresses’ silkworm dress has all used patterned embroidery; it is not ancient meaning.

units.zh: 今宜純服青，以為永制。」
units.en: Now it is fitting to wear plain green, taking it as permanent regulation.”
units.literal: Now it is fitting to wear pure green, taking it as permanent regulation.”

units.zh: 貴人、夫人、貴嬪，是為三夫人，皆金章紫綬，章文曰貴人、夫人、貴嬪之章。
units.en: The three chief consorts carry gold seals on purple ribbons.
units.literal: Honored lady, lady, honored concubine—these are the three consorts; all have gold seal purple sash; the seal text says honored lady, lady, honored concubine seals.

units.zh: 佩于闐玉。
units.en: They mount Khotan jade pendants.
units.literal: They wear Khotan jade.

units.zh: 淑妃、淑媛、淑儀、修華、修容、修儀、婕妤、容華、充華，是為九嬪，銀印青綬，佩采瓄玉。
units.en: Nine ranks of concubines wear silver seals, blue sashes, and mottled jade.
units.literal: Virtuous consort, virtuous beauty, virtuous deportment, cultivated splendor, cultivated countenance, cultivated deportment, lady of bright deportment, splendor countenance, filling splendor—these are the nine concubines; silver seal blue sash, wearing patterned jade.

units.zh: 貴人、貴嬪、夫人助蠶，服純縹為上與下，皆深衣制。
units.en: Chief ladies at the silkworm rite wear monochrome blue deep robes.
units.literal: Honored lady, honored concubine, and lady assisting at silkworm wear pure light blue above and below, all deep-robe system.

units.zh: 太平髻，七䥖蔽髻，黑玳瑁，又加簪珥。
units.en: Their hair towers in “great peace” buns with seven pins and tortoiseshell frames.
units.literal: Great peace topknot, seven-pin covering topknot, black tortoiseshell, again adding hairpins and earrings.

units.zh: 九嬪及公主、夫人五䥖，世婦三䥖。
units.en: Pin counts drop by rank—five or three jeweled skewers.
units.literal: Nine concubines and princesses and ladies five pins, noble wives three pins.

units.zh: 助蠶之義，自古而然矣。
units.en: Silkworm assistance is an immemorial duty of palace women.
units.literal: The meaning of assisting silkworm has been thus from antiquity.

units.zh: 皇太子妃金璽龜鈕，纁硃綬，佩瑜玉。
units.en: The crown princess matches princes’ tortoise seal and sash with fine jade.
units.literal: The heir apparent’s consort gold seal tortoise knob, reddish-cinnabar sash, wearing fine jade.

units.zh: 諸王太妃、妃、諸長公主、公主、封君金印紫綬，佩山玄玉。
units.en: Princely consorts and titled princesses share gold-on-purple with dark jade.
units.literal: Princes’ grand consorts and consorts, various senior princesses and princesses, and enfeoffed noblewomen have gold seal purple sash, wearing mountain-dark jade.

units.zh: 長公主、公主見會，太平髻，七䥖蔽髻。
units.en: At audiences princesses don the great-peace bun with seven jeweled pins.
units.literal: Senior princesses and princesses at meetings, great peace topknot, seven-pin covering topknot.

units.zh: 其長公主得有步搖，皆有簪珥，衣服同制。
units.en: Senior princesses who earn buyao tremblers also receive pins and earrings under the same wardrobe code.
units.literal: Their senior princesses may obtain buyao; all have hairpins and earrings; clothes share the same system.

units.zh: 自公主、封君以上皆帶綬，以彩組為緄帶，各如其綬色，金辟邪首為帶玦。
units.en: Princesses and titled noblewomen belt formal sashes with color-matched cord trim and gilded bixie belt toggles.
units.literal: From princesses and enfeoffed noblewomen upward all wear sashes; using colored cords as edge bands, each matching its sash color; golden bixie head as belt ring.

units.zh: 郡公侯縣公侯太夫人，夫人銀印青綬，佩水蒼玉，其特加乃金紫。
units.en: County and commandery ducal consorts normally wear silver on blue with aquamarine jade, unless promoted to gold-and-purple honors.
units.literal: Commandery dukes and marquises’ and county dukes’ and marquises’ grand ladies and ladies have silver seal blue sash, wearing water-green jade; if specially advanced then gold and purple.

units.zh: 公特進侯卿校世婦、中二千石二千石夫人紺繒幗，黃金龍首銜白珠，魚須擿長一尺為簪珥。
units.en: High ministers’ wives don dark gauze caps with gold dragon friezes, white pearls, and foot-long “fish-whisker” pins as earrings.
units.literal: Dukes fully eminent, marquises, ministers, colonels’ chief wives, and wives at full and regular two thousand piculs wear dark silk headcloths, yellow gold dragon heads holding white pearls, fish-whisker plucks one chi long as hairpins and earrings.

units.zh: 入廟佐祭者皁絹上下。
units.en: Women assisting temple sacrifice wear all-black silk deep robes.
units.literal: Those who enter the temple assisting sacrifice wear black silk above and below.

units.zh: 助蠶者縹絹上下，皆深衣制緣。
units.en: Silkworm helpers wear bordered light-blue deep gowns.
units.literal: Those assisting silkworm wear light-blue silk above and below, all deep-robe system with borders.

units.zh: 自二千石夫人以上至皇后，皆以蠶衣為朝服。
units.en: From senior ministers’ wives to the empress, formal court dress means the silkworm vestment set.
units.literal: From two thousand piculs’ wives upward to the empress, all take silkworm dress as court dress.
